Tom Izzo is not one to beat around the bush. He often takes blame for the Michigan State Spartans’ mistakes and struggles and calls it like he sees it.
So when the head coach found out ESPN commentator Dan Dakich insulted the Spartans’ fan base and the school’s education quality, he went on an uncensored rant.
In a since-deleted tweet, Dakich – whose son, Andrew, is a senior guard for the Michigan Wolverines – said “Sparty not only whines but now just dumb!! Couldn’t get into UM??” In more Twitter exchanges, he repeatedly called MSU fans whiners.
@sportz5176 @budrowley that's great but sweetheart nobody whines like Sparty!!! — Dan Dakich (@dandakich) February 8, 2017
And that led to MSU’s Izzone student section chanting, “We hate Dakich” throughout the Spartans’ 74-66 win over Ohio State on Tuesday – a game he was calling for ESPN.
When Izzo got some context for the chants, he went off.
Via the Detroit Free Press:
“If I would have known that before the game, I would have embarrassed myself almost as much as he embarrassed himself, and I would have led the chants,” Izzo said, his voice slightly cracking. “Because calling us whiners and that is kind of unprofessional. Classy broadcasters, like George Blaha and everybody else, wouldn’t have even thought to do something like that on TV. But saying our students couldn’t get in there? And he’s doing games for Michigan when his son is there? That is a disappointment, and that is ridiculous. “And I think it’s funny because I got no respect for him for that. And I am going to publicly say it – you can tweet it, you can read it, you can do whatever you want with it – but Twitter got him in trouble, and he earned it. I am surprised ESPN would let somebody say something like that, that works for them.”
He also added that he “would have loved” to join the Izzone in chanting and said he owes MSU fans and students an apology – but acknowleded he probably won’t get it.
rewrite:
Known for his directness, Michigan State Spartans head coach Tom Izzo rarely minces words, frequently accepting responsibility for his team’s errors and offering blunt assessments. Therefore, it was no surprise when he launched into a frank and impassioned response after learning of ESPN commentator Dan Dakich’s derogatory remarks about the Spartans’ fan base and the university’s academic standing. Dakich, whose son plays for the rival Michigan Wolverines, posted a since-deleted tweet stating, “Sparty not only whines but now just dumb!! Couldn’t get into UM??” He further engaged in Twitter exchanges, repeatedly labeling MSU fans as whiners.

This incident fueled the Izzone, Michigan State’s student section, to chant “We hate Dakich” during the Spartans’ 74-66 victory over Ohio State on Tuesday—a game Dakich was broadcasting for ESPN. Upon understanding the reason for the chants, Izzo did not hold back. His voice slightly cracking with emotion, he expressed his disdain for Dakich’s comments. “If I would have known that before the game, I would have embarrassed myself almost as much as he embarrassed himself, and I would have led the chants,” Izzo stated. He criticized the remarks as unprofessional, contrasting Dakich with classier broadcasters like George Blaha who would never make such statements on air.

Izzo took particular issue with the insinuation about his students’ academic qualifications, as well as the apparent conflict of interest given Dakich’s son plays for Michigan while Dakich covers games involving the rival school. “That is a disappointment, and that is ridiculous,” Izzo said. He made a point to publicly declare his lost respect for Dakich, adding, “Twitter got him in trouble, and he earned it.” Izzo also expressed surprise that ESPN would permit an employee to make such comments. Furthermore, he admitted he “would have loved” to join the student chants and believes an apology is owed to the MSU community, though he acknowledged one is unlikely to be forthcoming.

These actions align with our mission Barry Craig

FILE PHOTO: The seal of the Department of Commerce is pictured in Washington, D.C., U.S. March 10, 2017. REUTERS/Eric Thayer
WASHINGTON The U.S. Commerce Department is launching a new review of whether China should be treated as a market economy country, a designation that would effectively limit the calculation of anti-dumping duties on China-made goods.
Buried in a federal notice on Wednesday about an investigation into alleged dumping of Chinese aluminum foil into the U.S. market, the department said it is seeking public comments on China's non-market economy status.
The review comes as the White House prepares for the first face-to-face meeting between President Donald Trump and China's President Xi Jinping on April 6-7 at Trump's Mar-a-Lago retreat in Florida.
China's non-market economy status is considered an irritant for Beijing as the Trump administration works on trade policies aimed at reducing the flow of Chinese imports in to the United States.
When China joined the World Trade Organization in 2001, its accession terms allowed other WTO members to treat it as a non-market economy and use a third country's prices to assess whether Chinese goods were being sold below cost.
But part of that clause expired on Dec. 11, 2016, which China says means WTO trading partners must drop their use of such surrogate pricing, which has led to higher U.S. anti-dumping duties on imported Chinese goods.
The United States and European Union failed to change their view of China's status. A day later, Beijing launched a formal complaint against them before the WTO.
The Commerce Department last conducted a review of China's non-market economy status in 2006, determining that China failed on all six determining criteria, which are:
* the extent to which the country's currency is convertible into other currencies;
* the extent to which wage rates are determined by free bargaining by labor and management;
* the extent to which joint ventures or other investments by foreign firms are permitted in the country;
* the extent of government ownership or control of the means of production;
* the extent of government control over allocation of resources and over price and output decisions of enterprises, and
* other factors the administering authority considers appropriate.
(Reporting by David Lawder, editing by G Crosse)
rewrite:
In Washington, D.C., the Department of Commerce seal was photographed on March 10, 2017. The U.S. Commerce Department has initiated a fresh evaluation regarding China's classification as a market economy nation. Such a designation would restrict how anti-dumping duties on Chinese products are computed. This review was announced in a federal notice on Wednesday concerning an inquiry into suspected dumping of Chinese aluminum foil in the United States. Within that notice, the department requested public input on China's non-market economy standing.

This development coincides with preparations for the inaugural in-person meeting between President Donald Trump and China's President Xi Jinping, scheduled for April 6-7 at Trump's Mar-a-Lago estate in Florida. Beijing views the non-market economy label as a persistent annoyance, especially as the Trump administration crafts trade policies intended to curb Chinese imports.

Upon joining the World Trade Organization in 2001, China's terms of entry permitted other WTO members to classify it as a non-market economy. This allowed the use of prices from a third country to determine if Chinese goods were being sold at unfairly low prices. However, a segment of this provision lapsed on December 11, 2016. China contends that this expiration obligates WTO partners to cease using such surrogate pricing, a method that has resulted in elevated U.S. anti-dumping duties on Chinese imports.

Neither the United States nor the European Union altered their stance on China's status following that date. In response, Beijing filed a formal complaint with the WTO against them the next day. The Commerce Department previously examined China's non-market economy status in 2006, concluding at that time that China did not meet any of the six established criteria. These criteria encompass: the convertibility of the country's currency; how wage rates are set through bargaining between labor and management; the permissions granted for foreign joint ventures or investments; the degree of government ownership or control over production means; the level of government control over resource allocation and enterprise decisions on pricing and output; and any other factors deemed relevant by the administering authority.

TORONTO — Ontario's premier said she'd welcome U.S. President Donald Trump's education secretary to visit the province's public schools if she chooses to reschedule a cancelled trip, even though she disagrees with some of Betsy DeVos' positions.
Kathleen Wynne said Friday that she was looking forward to an opportunity to show DeVos a strong, publicly funded education system.
DeVos cancelled a planned visit for Thursday and Friday this week just one day in advance, citing "scheduling issues," though the U.S. Department of Education noted the trip had merely been postponed.
The visit had caused some controversy in Ontario, where teachers' unions expressed concerns over DeVos' advocacy for school choice, including vouchers that allow kids to attend publicly funded but privately operated charter schools, or private schools on the public dime.
The NDP called on the government to not allow DeVos to tour schools in the province — a position Wynne said she doesn't understand.
"I don't agree with the positions that Secretary DeVos has taken in the past, that's true, but I think that's all the more reason to have an opportunity to showcase what we do in our schools and how strong a publicly funded education system can be," Wynne said Friday.
"So I honestly don't understand why we would want to hide that under a bushel. I would think we'd want to celebrate the success of our publicly funded education system."
DeVos has also attracted protests recently for revoking a guidance that instructed colleges on how to handle sexual assault cases, saying the previous policy was unfairly skewed against those accused of assault, and for the department of education rolling back rules allowing transgender students to use school restrooms of their choice.
Wynne has advocated for protections for LGBT Ontarians and her government launched a large campaign aimed at ending sexual harassment and violence.
Despite differences of opinion, Wynne said she would want to display Ontario's education system.
rewrite:
Ontario Premier Kathleen Wynne stated on Friday that she would welcome U.S. Education Secretary Betsy DeVos to visit the province’s public schools should the trip be rescheduled, despite disagreeing with many of DeVos’s policy stances. Wynne expressed eagerness for an opportunity to showcase Ontario’s robust, publicly funded education system.

DeVos cancelled a planned visit scheduled for Thursday and Friday of this week with just one day’s notice, attributing the change to “scheduling issues.” The U.S. Department of Education indicated the trip was postponed rather than cancelled entirely. The prospect of the visit had already stirred controversy within Ontario, where teachers’ unions raised concerns over DeVos’s advocacy for school choice programs. These include voucher systems that enable students to attend privately operated charter schools or private institutions using public funds.

The provincial NDP called on the government to deny DeVos access to Ontario schools—a position Wynne said she finds puzzling. “I don’t agree with the positions that Secretary DeVos has taken in the past, that’s true, but I think that’s all the more reason to have an opportunity to showcase what we do in our schools and how strong a publicly funded education system can be,” Wynne remarked. She added, “So I honestly don’t understand why we would want to hide that under a bushel. I would think we’d want to celebrate the success of our publicly funded education system.”

DeVos has recently drawn protests for several actions, including revoking guidance to colleges on handling sexual assault cases—arguing prior policy unfairly treated the accused—and for the Education Department rolling back rules that allowed transgender students to use restrooms matching their gender identity. Wynne, who has advocated for protections for LGBT Ontarians and launched a major campaign against sexual harassment and violence, emphasized that despite these differences, she would still wish to present Ontario’s educational achievements.

rewrite:
In response to recent vehicle attacks, some festivals and markets have begun positioning garbage and fire trucks at their entrances as a safety barrier. This approach mirrors measures taken in Toronto on Monday night, where streets were closed near the Air Canada Centre during an NHL playoff game for the Maple Leafs. Security expert Mubin Shaikh, reflecting on such incidents, expressed that a "no rental" list would be a largely reactive measure with minimal real impact. He argues that determined attackers, if restricted from rentals, could simply borrow or steal vehicles instead. "A criminal will try to take whatever they can, however they can," Shaikh notes, adding, "Will it deter the determined attacker? Probably not."

Shaikh, a counterterrorism specialist from Toronto, learned of Monday's tragedy upon landing at a German air force base, where he was scheduled to brief officials on vehicle-based attacks. "Unfortunately, this is the reality in which we live nowadays," he said. He described becoming hyper-vigilant in public, constantly scanning for protective structures like cement planters or pillars to duck behind should a vehicle mount the curb. Ultimately, he acknowledges the profound difficulty of prevention: "At the end of the day, it's impossible (to prevent). We live in an open society and vehicles are in our proximity all the time. That's normal city life."

Meanwhile, according to reports, several vehicles used in recent attacks have been rentals, prompting consideration of a potential registry to help prevent similar events. However, as noted, the specific form such a database would take remains unclear.

The Chicago woman who live streamed the racially charged beating of a white Chicago teen with mental disabilities, pleaded guilty to hate crimes and was sentenced to just 4 years probation this Friday.
Brittany Covington, 19, has been in custody since her arrest in January.
Cook County Circuit Judge William Hooks called the event “horrific” and banned Covington from using social media for her 4 years of probation. Covington was also banned from communicating with the other two co-defendants, and she has been ordered 200 hours of community service.
Hooks told Covington he could have imposed a prison sentence but added, “I’m not sure if I did that you’d be coming out any better.”
I disagree, and I’m sure the parents of that disabled child, and other families would agree. This disabled child was lured from school to an empty apartment where he could be tied up and brutalized on camera just because he was white, this certainly calls for jail time. This 19 year old girl should not be allowed back in society if this is the type of damage she is capable of causing.
She clearly wasn’t thinking about the repercussions of her actions in the slightest if she was live streaming the crime on Facebook, which is scary, a young woman who is willing to commit a crime this heinous should be removed from society until she can learn to live with others.
Three others were charged in the incident: alleged ringleader Jordan Hill, 19, as well as Tesfaye Cooper, 19, and Covington’s sister, Tanishia, 25. Their cases are still pending.
All of these young adults deserve to spend time behind bars for this disgusting act of violence and racism. There is clearly a deep seeded anger here for the white population that isn’t going to be solved with 4 years off Facebook, these young adults need help, and need to be removed from society.
rewrite:
This Friday, Brittany Covington, a 19-year-old Chicago woman, pleaded guilty to hate crimes and received a sentence of four years probation. She had been in custody since her arrest in January for live streaming the racially charged beating of a white teenager with mental disabilities. Cook County Circuit Judge William Hooks described the incident as “horrific.” As part of her probation, Covington is banned from using social media and from communicating with her two co-defendants; she must also complete 200 hours of community service.

Judge Hooks stated that while he could have imposed a prison sentence, he was not convinced it would lead to her improvement. I strongly disagree with this leniency, as I believe the victim’s parents and many others would as well. The disabled teen was lured from school to an empty apartment, where he was tied up and brutally assaulted on camera specifically because of his race. Such a premeditated and hate-driven act unquestionably warrants jail time. A 19-year-old capable of this degree of cruelty should not be permitted back into society.

The fact that she broadcast the crime on Facebook demonstrates a complete disregard for the consequences of her actions. It is alarming that a young woman would commit such a heinous act, and she should be separated from society until she can learn to coexist with others. Three other individuals—alleged ringleader Jordan Hill, 19, Tesfaye Cooper, 19, and Covington’s sister, Tanishia, 25—have also been charged, and their cases remain pending.

All these young adults deserve incarceration for this disgusting act of violent racism. Their actions reveal a deep-seated anger toward white people that cannot be addressed by merely restricting social media access for a few years. These individuals require serious intervention and must be removed from society.

JOHANNESBURG - Growthpoint Properties, the largest South African real estate investment trust (Reit) listed on the JSE with assets on three continents, has established a dedicated trading and development business unit.
Estienne de Klerk, the chief executive of Growthpoint South Africa, said yesterday that the new specialised division would play a key role in creating excellent business opportunities for the company and world-class premises for its clients.
Until now, Growthpoint’s in-house trading and development skills were held within each sector of the company’s portfolio, including office, retail and industrial. The new business unit would combine and integrate Growthpoint’s cross-sector development and trading expertise to optimise its business strengths.
De Klerk said the new business unit would enable Growthpoint to provide their clients with an extra service that met their needs. “Besides providing existing buildings, we can create new buildings for them that meet their very specific, bespoke requirements.”
De Klerk added that Growthpoint’s trading and development team was a key part of their business and had played a significant role in building the company’s portfolio. He said Growthpoint’s goal was to generate consistent, recurring income from third-party development fees and trading profit that totalled no more than 1percent to 2percent of its distributable income.
Rudolf Pienaar, the new chief investment and development officer at Growthpoint, said development played a key role in Growthpoint’s South African investment strategy with tailor-made assets designed to enhance its portfolio and retain and attract quality clients.
However, Pienaar said that in working closely with its clients Growthpoint had found that some of their needs went beyond a simple tenancy. He said their company policy may require them to own certain types of properties; they might need to dispose of a property asset to become a tenant of Growthpoint, or they could require specialised premises that could only be custom-developed.
- BUSINESS REPORT
rewrite:
Growthpoint Properties, the largest South African real estate investment trust (Reit) listed on the JSE and holding assets across three continents, has formed a new, dedicated business unit focused on trading and development. According to Estienne de Klerk, chief executive of Growthpoint South Africa, this specialised division is designed to generate excellent opportunities for the company while delivering world-class premises for clients. Previously, the company’s development and trading capabilities were distributed across different portfolio sectors—office, retail, and industrial. The new unit will consolidate this cross-sector expertise to optimise business strengths.

De Klerk explained that the unit allows Growthpoint to offer an additional service tailored to client needs. Beyond supplying existing buildings, the company can now develop new, bespoke properties that meet specific requirements. He emphasised that the trading and development team has been fundamental in building Growthpoint’s portfolio. A key objective is to produce steady, recurring income from third-party development fees and trading profits, targeting a contribution of between 1% and 2% of distributable income.

Rudolf Pienaar, Growthpoint’s chief investment and development officer, noted that development is central to the company’s South African investment strategy, creating tailor-made assets to enhance its portfolio and attract high-quality clients. Pienaar added that close engagement with clients has revealed needs that extend beyond standard leasing arrangements. Some clients, due to corporate policy, may need to own certain property types; others might seek to sell an asset before becoming a Growthpoint tenant, or they could require specially developed premises that are not available on the open market.

By Charles Kumolu
IRKED by the poor power supply in the country, the Nigerian Young Professionals Forum, NYPF, has concluded plans to hold a two-day workshop for host community youth leaders where power stations and pipeline installations are located across the country.
A statement by the convener of the event, scheduled to hold from September 25 to 26 in Abuja, NYPF, Mr. Moses Siasia, said the move became important given the need to engage key actors in the sabotage of the power sector, who had contributed to Nigeria’s less than 3,000 megawatts generating status.
His words: “This shameful act of sabotage is mainly caused by youths of our generation, who have lost faith and do not see themselves as stakeholders in our society.
“It is imperative to note with our recent findings that it is only few stakeholders and players in the power sector that is concerned about finding a solution to this menace, while some see it as a cash cow because of their selfish interests.
“But for us as NYPF, we see it as an opportunity to contribute our quota towards nation building. At the end of the workshop, participants will be strategically engaged as volunteers for proper security of the nation’s power assets for effective and efficient increased power supply and service delivery.”
rewrite:
In response to Nigeria's inadequate power supply, the Nigerian Young Professionals Forum (NYPF) has organized a two-day workshop for youth leaders from communities hosting power stations and pipeline installations nationwide. The event, set for September 25–26 in Abuja, aims to address key actors involved in sabotaging the power sector—a major factor limiting the country's generation to under 3,000 megawatts. According to a statement by NYPF convener Mr. Moses Siasia, this initiative is crucial for engaging those whose actions have severely undermined national infrastructure.

Siasia emphasized, "This shameful act of sabotage is mainly caused by youths of our generation, who have lost faith and do not see themselves as stakeholders in our society." He further noted that recent findings reveal only a limited number of power sector stakeholders are genuinely committed to solving this problem, while others exploit it for personal gain. "But for us as NYPF," he stated, "we see it as an opportunity to contribute our quota towards nation building."

Following the workshop, participants will be strategically deployed as volunteers to help secure the nation's power assets. The goal is to enhance security, promote more effective and efficient power supply, and improve overall service delivery.

Giancarlo Stanton said to be ‘very happy’ over trade to Yankees
Giancarlo Stanton may have had to settle on less than his first choice when he accepted a trade to the New York Yankees, but he is apparently excited about his new home.
Jon Heyman of FanRag Sports spoke with a friend of Stanton, and the 28-year-old slugger is said to be “very happy” that he will be wearing pinstripes next season.
Giancarlo Stanton, who’s passed his physical and is officially a Yankee, is said by a friend to be “very happy” with how it turned out. Press conferrence is at 2 et tomorrow. — Jon Heyman (@JonHeyman) December 11, 2017
There were rumblings earlier in the offseason that Stanton wanted to play on the west coast, which is why the San Francisco Giants were considered the favorite. It also seems like Stanton had a clear-cut top choice on his wish list, but getting a chance to play for one of the most storied franchises in sports in one of the biggest markets in the country is a nice consolation prize.
With Stanton and Aaron Judge in the middle of their lineup, the Yankees should be perennial title contenders once again.

While earlier offseason rumors suggested Stanton preferred a move to the west coast, with the San Francisco Giants seen as the frontrunner, the outcome has evidently pleased him. Although it may not have been his absolute first choice, the opportunity to join one of sports' most historic franchises in a major market represents a significant consolation. Stanton, who has passed his physical and is now officially a Yankee, is set to be introduced at a press conference scheduled for 2 p.m. ET tomorrow. His addition to a lineup that already features Aaron Judge positions the Yankees as perennial contenders for championships once again. Ultimately, despite possibly settling for less than his initial preference, Stanton is reportedly excited about his new team and the prospects it brings.

Russian Olympic Committee President Alexander Zhukov has praised the performances of the 19 athletes from his country who competed as neutrals at the International Association of Athletics Federations (IAAF) World Championships here.
Russians were forced to take part under the Authorised Neutral Athletes (ANA) banner because country has been banned from international competition by the IAAF since November 2015 following allegations of state-supported doping.
The team won a total of six medals to finish ninth in the overall medals table, finishing ahead of Germany, Australia and Jamaica.
Russian athletes actually won more medals competing as ANA than they did at the previous World Championships in Beijing two years ago when, under their own flag, they collected four.
Their medals total at London was made up of one gold and five silver.
The gold medal was won by Mariya Lasitskene in the high jump, successfully defending the title she won had won in Beijing in 2015 under her maiden name Kuchina.
"One gold and five silver medals," Zhukov told Russia's official state news agency TASS.
"Half of the team could count on medals."
Zhukov added: "Under such conditions, these are remarkable results."
"I believe that, if we take the overall psychological factor, the fact that we have not won medals at international competitions for a long time, that most of the athletes came without their coaches, and that does make an impact, they performed very well.
"I want to congratulate all our athletes."
Besides Lasitskene, other Russians to win medals at London included Danil Lysenko.
He won a silver medal during the final session last night in the men's high jump.
Other silver medals were won by Sergey Shubenkov in the 110 metres hurdles, Darya Klishina in the women's long jump, Valeriy Pronkin in the men's hammer throw and Sergei Shirokobokov in the men's 20 kilometres walk.
rewrite:
At the International Association of Athletics Federations (IAAF) World Championships in London, the 19 Russian athletes competing as Authorised Neutral Athletes (ANA) secured a total of six medals, placing ninth overall in the standings ahead of nations like Germany, Australia, and Jamaica. Russian Olympic Committee President Alexander Zhukov lauded these performances, noting the challenging circumstances under which the team competed. Due to allegations of state-supported doping, Russia has been banned from international athletics by the IAAF since November 2015, forcing its athletes to participate under a neutral banner rather than their national flag.

The medal haul consisted of one gold and five silver medals, surpassing the four medals Russia earned at the previous World Championships in Beijing in 2015. Zhukov, speaking to the official state news agency TASS, remarked, "One gold and five silver medals," and added, "Half of the team could count on medals." He emphasized the significance of these results given the context: "Under such conditions, these are remarkable results." Zhukov pointed to psychological factors, including a prolonged absence from international podiums and the absence of personal coaches for many athletes, as hurdles that made their achievements particularly commendable. He concluded, "I believe that, if we take the overall psychological factor... they performed very well. I want to congratulate all our athletes."

The sole gold was claimed by high jumper Mariya Lasitskene, who successfully defended the title she originally won in Beijing under her maiden name, Kuchina. Silver medals were earned by Danil Lysenko in the men’s high jump, Sergey Shubenkov in the 110-meter hurdles, Darya Klishina in the women’s long jump, Valeriy Pronkin in the men’s hammer throw, and Sergei Shirokobokov in the men’s 20-kilometer walk. This collective effort highlighted the team’s resilience despite competing without national representation.

Joey Badass, who’s got a busy summer ahead of him as he kicks off his Amerikkkana Tour alongside Compton rappers Buddy and Boogie, has announced the date of the 4th annual Steez Day Music Festival at Central Park’s Summerstage in New York City featuring Joey himself along with his crew Pro Era, as well as fellow Beast Coast crew members Flatbush Zombies and The Underachievers, and affiliated Brooklyn MC Stro.
Steez Day Festival is just one festival that has been started in honor of a fallen up-and-coming rap luminary by his surviving crew mates, with ASAP Mob following in Pro Era’s footsteps with their own Yams Day. Unfortunately, the 2017 Yams Day Festival was shut down due to attendees brawling.
Hopefully, Steez Day won’t be marred by bellicose fans, as it’s meant to be a celebration of the life of Pro Era and Beast Coast member Capital Steez, who committed suicide on Christmas Eve in 2012, sending shockwaves through New York’s then-burgeoning next-wave underground rap scene. It was Steez who initially coined the name for the extended crew including The Underachievers and Flatbush Zombies, and was known for his precocious, socially conscious lyrics.
Unfortunately, Steez wasn’t around to witness the eventual success of his crew members, as Joey’s album All-Amerikkkan Badass rewrote the book on throwback, lyrical rap and Flatbush Zombies’ new album Vacation In Hell constituted a rip-roaring comeback for a crew that had been relatively quiet for a few years.
The 4th annual Steez Day 2018 will take over Central Park July 8. Tickets will be available this Friday, April 27.
rewrite:
The 4th annual Steez Day Music Festival will be held at Central Park’s Summerstage in New York City on July 8, 2018. Organized by Joey Badass, the event will feature performances by his crew Pro Era, fellow Beast Coast members Flatbush Zombies and The Underachievers, and affiliated Brooklyn MC Stro. This announcement comes as Joey prepares for a busy summer, launching his Amerikkkana Tour with Compton rappers Buddy and Boogie.

Steez Day honors Capital Steez, a Pro Era and Beast Coast member who died by suicide on Christmas Eve in 2012. His death profoundly impacted New York’s burgeoning underground rap scene at the time. Capital Steez was recognized for his precocious, socially conscious lyrics and is credited with coining the name for the extended crew that included The Underachievers and Flatbush Zombies.

Like the ASAP Mob’s Yams Day, which followed this example, Steez Day is a festival created by surviving crew mates to memorialize a fallen rap luminary. Organizers hope the event remains a peaceful celebration, avoiding disruptions such as those that led to the shutdown of the 2017 Yams Day Festival due to attendee brawls.

Tragically, Steez did not live to see the subsequent successes of his peers. These include Joey Badass’s acclaimed album *All-Amerikkkan Badass*, which redefined lyrical throwback rap, and Flatbush Zombies’ vigorous comeback album *Vacation In Hell* after a period of relative quiet. Tickets for the 2018 Steez Day Festival go on sale Friday, April 27.

“Friday’s news of Apple’s permit to test self-driving cars in California should not have come as much of a surprise given the poorly kept secret of Project Titan,” Gene Munster writes for Loup Ventures. “But the permit begs the question of whether Apple is building a car or just building software for a car.”
“In an ideal world, Apple’s car project would involve the company building the actual automobile, combining hardware and software,” Munster writes. “In reality, the complexity of designing and manufacturing a vehicle may push the company to integrate deeply with an automotive partner or partners in an effort more similar to the Apple TV — plugging Apple’s technology into an existing product.”
“Apple is almost certainly exploring how it could build an entire car, but as we learned the hard way with an Apple television, exploration does not mean a product comes to market,” Munster writes. “Apple is the best connected device maker in the world and the car is the biggest connected device in the world.”
Read more in the full article here.
rewrite: According to Gene Munster of Loup Ventures, Apple's recent permit to test autonomous vehicles in California, announced Friday, was hardly unexpected due to the long-rumored "Project Titan." However, this development raises a critical question: is Apple aiming to manufacture a full car or only to develop its software? Munster notes that ideally, Apple would create the entire vehicle, merging its hardware and software expertise. Yet the immense complexity of automotive design and production might instead lead the company to pursue deep integration with an established automotive partner, akin to the Apple TV model—essentially fitting Apple's technology into a pre-existing product. While Apple is undoubtedly investigating how to build a complete car, Munster cautions that such exploration, as the abandoned Apple television project demonstrated, does not guarantee a market release. He concludes by observing that Apple is the world's premier connected device maker, and the car represents the ultimate connected device.

The Boss is Broadway bound.
Bruce Springsteen will make his Broadway debut at the Walter Kerr Theatre for an eight-week run in the fall, The Post has learned exclusively.
Sources say Springsteen will do a pared-down version of the set he usually performs in huge arenas and stadiums all over the world.
“He wants to play a smaller house,” a theater source says. “He wants to try something more intimate, and he likes the idea of being on Broadway.”
Dates haven’t been finalized, but Springsteen will likely open in November. He’ll perform five times a week. Jujamcyn Theaters, which owns the Kerr, gave him a sweetheart deal he couldn’t refuse: no rent for the eight weeks.
The 975-seat Kerr has been empty since the musical “Amélie” closed in May.
“He’ll keep the lights on in the building, and they’ll sell gazillions of dollars worth of booze,” a source says.
Springsteen will sell out the run in a minute, though whatever he makes will pale in comparison to the tens of millions of dollars he makes on tour.
But as one music source says: “He’s got all the money in the world. He can do what he likes.”
Some insiders believe Springsteen’s Broadway gig may be a curtain raiser to another project — turning his best-selling memoir, “Born To Run,” into a musical. Several producers, dollar signs dancing in their eyes, approached Springsteen about adapting the book for the stage after The Post reported he was interested in the idea.
It could be a blockbuster along the lines of “Jersey Boys” and “Beautiful: the Carole King Musical.”
But that’s a long way off. In the meantime, you’ll be able to see the Boss “live and in person” at the Kerr this fall.
rewrite:

According to sources, he plans to present a more intimate, pared-down version of the arena and stadium sets for which he is globally known. “He wants to play a smaller house,” a theater source explains. “He wants to try something more intimate, and he likes the idea of being on Broadway.”

While dates are not yet finalized, the run is expected to begin in November, with Springsteen performing five shows per week. Jujamcyn Theaters, owner of the Walter Kerr, has offered an enticing arrangement: no rent for the entire eight weeks. The 975-seat theater has been vacant since the musical “Amélie” closed in May. “He’ll keep the lights on in the building, and they’ll sell gazillions of dollars worth of booze,” a source notes.

The engagement is certain to sell out instantly, though the revenue will likely pale next to the tens of millions he earns on major tours. But as one music insider observes, “He’s got all the money in the world. He can do what he likes.”

Some speculate this Broadway stint may serve as a precursor to another venture: adapting his best-selling memoir, “Born To Run,” into a musical. After The Post reported his interest, several producers have approached him about the idea, envisioning a potential blockbuster similar to “Jersey Boys” or “Beautiful: the Carole King Musical.” However, that project remains a distant possibility. For now, audiences will have the chance to see the Boss live and in person at the Kerr this autumn.

The USMNT takes on Panama tonight on ESPN 2 in a pivotal World Cup qualifying match. ESPN’s pre-match coverage begins at 7 p.m. Eastern, while the match officially kicks off at 7:35 p.m. Eastern. Heavy will have the starting XI for both teams as soon as they are announced.
Heading into the match, Panama sits in third in the hex with 10 points, while the USA is in fourth with nine points.
The top three teams clinch a 2018 World Cup qualifying birth. The fourth-place team will play in a playoff game against Asia’s fifth-place team with the winner clinching a spot. So far, Mexico is the only team in the hex to have clinched a spot for 2018.
Three of the last four USA-Panama matches have ended in a draw with another 2015 match requiring penalty kicks to decide the winner. The United States have been in a bit of a slump. They reached a draw with Honduras the last time out, and lost to Costa Rica in the match prior.
Panama is coming off a 3-0 win in September over Trinidad and Tobago. USMNT’s coach Bruce Arena understands the importance of the national team qualifying for the World Cup. Arena spoke with Sports Illustrated’s Grant Wahl on the World Cup’s importance.
“It’s very important [to make the World Cup],” Arena told Sports Illustrated. “We continue to grow the game in this country. I think the game in the United States is at its highest point in its history with a growing domestic league, a very competitive national team and a region that continues to grow as well. It’s important that we continue to qualify for World Cups.”
All this leads to the United States final qualifying match on Tuesday, October 10 against Trinidad & Tobago. The USMNT earning three points tonight would ease some of the pressure heading into Tuesday’s match.
We’ll have both starting lineups as soon as they are released.

In the standings, Panama currently occupies third place in the hexagonal final round with 10 points, while the United States follows closely in fourth with nine points. The top three teams from this stage secure automatic qualification for the 2018 World Cup. The fourth-place finisher must enter a playoff against the fifth-place team from Asia, with the victor claiming a final spot. To date, Mexico is the only team from the region to have officially clinched its place for 2018.

The recent history between these sides suggests a tight contest; three of their last four encounters have ended in draws, with a 2015 match even requiring penalty kicks to determine a winner. The United States enters this match seeking improved form, having drawn with Honduras in its last outing and fallen to Costa Rica before that. Conversely, Panama approaches the game with momentum from a 3-0 victory over Trinidad and Tobago in September.

USMNT head coach Bruce Arena has emphasized the critical importance of World Cup qualification for the nation’s soccer growth. I think the game in the United States is at its highest point in its history with a growing domestic league, a very competitive national team and a region that continues to grow as well. It’s important that we continue to qualify for World Cups.”

The outcome of tonight’s match carries significant weight for the United States’ final qualifier on Tuesday, October 10, against Trinidad & Tobago. Securing three points against Panama would substantially alleviate the pressure heading into that decisive fixture. The starting elevens for both teams will be published as soon as they are available.

LOGAN, Ohio — One match can make all the difference.
The Gallia Academy wrestling team claimed a narrow victory over non-conference host Logan on Thursday at Jim Myers Gymnasium, defeating the Chieftains by a 42-37 count in a dual meet.
The Blue Devils won four matches by pinfall and three more by forfeit.
Gallia Academy’s pinfall victories came from junior Kenton Ramsey in the 113-pound matchup, junior Justin Day at 132 pounds, sophomore Bronson Carter in the 138 class, and junior Boo Pullins at 182.
Winning by forfeit for GAHS were seniors Caleb Greenlee (106), Kyle Greenlee (120), and Hunter Terry (285).
In the 160 match for Gallia Academy, Kenny Siders dropped a 9-2 decision, while in the 170 class Andrew Mullins lost a major, 16-4, decision.
GAHS surrendered the the 220 class by forfeit, while Grant Bryan (126), Corbin Walker (145), Austin Peroud (152) and Nickolas Hufford (195) suffered pinfall defeats.
The Blue Devils are set to wrestle again on Wednesday at Meigs.

Tom Brady will be sidelined Super Bowl Sunday.
“It’s my day off,” the 22-year-old Staten Island pizza deliveryman told The Post.
The die-hard Jets fan will spend the day rooting hard against his namesake instead.
“Enough is enough. … The Patriots win too many Super Bowls.”
Brady is just one of 31 Tom Bradys living in New York City, with at least one in every borough.
You’re most likely to bump and run into a Tom Brady in Brooklyn, where 11 reside. There are five in the Bronx, four on Staten Island and two in Queens. There are nine listed in Manhattan, including the one married to Brazilian supermodel Gisele Bundchen and living in a $14 million apartment at One Madison in the Flatiron District.
Like the pretty boy quarterback, Staten Island Tom Brady’s father is of Irish descent, while his mom has Polish roots.
“I even have his middle name — Edward. It’s a curse and it’s a blessing,” said Brady.
“Every time I meet new people they say, ‘Are you related to Tom Brady?’ I’ve messed around with a couple of people and said, ‘Yeah, I’m his nephew.’ Some people fall for it,” he laughed.
Staten Island Tom, who cuts lawns in the summer, doesn’t have the NFL superstar’s $180 million net worth, but he does have his confidence.
“Tell Gisele if she ever gets tired … I’m 6-2 and single,” he quipped.
Tom Brady from Queens is no lookalike. The 69-year-old tour bus driver, at 5-foot-9 and 260 pounds, is built more for the couch than the gridiron.
“I’m Tom Brady and I have air in my footballs,” he joked.
He’s even driven the Patriots around town but can’t recall if his namesake was aboard his bus because “I don’t have any interest in football.”
For Eagles fans keeping score, there are zero Nick Foles listed in the city.

universities in Leeds have made almost £400,000 from fining students for overdue library books in the past three years.
Leeds University accrued the most money from overdue books, collecting more than £211,000 in fines since the 2014/2015 academic year.
Leeds Beckett, which collected £147,509, was the second highest, while Leeds Trinity University was third with fines totalling £27,682
A spokesperson for the University of Leeds said: “The university has five libraries and nearly 33,000 students, so our size is a factor in any comparison of library fines, and all fines are invested back into our libraries.”
With fines as little as 10p a day for each day a book is overdue, it shows that students are returning thousands of books late each year.
The universities say that all the fines are ploughed back into library services, with money spent on resources, including books and journals, “that it is benefited directly by the student”.
A spokesperson for Leeds Beckett University said: “Fines are used as a strategy to ensure the prompt return of books and to maximise book availability for all students in a context of sharing resources. Staff are also charged fines at the same level.
“Students generally support the use of fines to encourage their fellow students to bring back books promptly so they all get a chance to use them.”
Students at the University of Leeds only start incurring fines if the borrowed book has been requested by someone else, and they must then fork out £2.50 per day if the item is overdue.
A Leeds University Union spokesperson said: “The cost of student living is an ongoing conversation between us and the university. We will continue to work with the libraries to ensure that students are kept well informed on policies and procedures that may lead to fines and that these are fair and transparent.”
rewrite:
Over the past three years, fines for overdue library books have generated nearly £400,000 for universities in Leeds. Leading this figure is the University of Leeds, which accrued more than £211,000 in such fines since the 2014/2015 academic year. Following next was Leeds Beckett University, collecting £147,509, while Leeds Trinity University ranked third with total fines of £27,682. Given that daily fines can be as minimal as 10p per overdue book, these substantial totals indicate that thousands of books are returned late by students each year.

According to the institutions, all fine revenue is reinvested directly into library services. This funding supports resources like books and journals, which directly benefit the student body. A University of Leeds spokesperson highlighted their scale, noting, “The university has five libraries and nearly 33,000 students, so our size is a factor in any comparison of library fines.” Similarly, a Leeds Beckett University spokesperson explained, “Fines are used as a strategy to ensure the prompt return of books and to maximise book availability for all students in a context of sharing resources.” The same fines apply to staff members. The spokesperson added, “Students generally support the use of fines to encourage their fellow students to bring back books promptly so they all get a chance to use them.”

At the University of Leeds, fines are only triggered when a borrowed book has been requested by another user; thereafter, the charge is £2.50 per day for an overdue item. Addressing the broader financial context, a Leeds University Union spokesperson stated, “The cost of student living is an ongoing conversation between us and the university. We will continue to work with the libraries to ensure that students are kept well informed on policies and procedures that may lead to fines and that these are fair and transparent.”

A Ventura backpacker missing for more than a day in Los Padres National Forest northeast of Lake Cachuma was rescued Saturday night by a Santa Barbara County Sheriff’s Department helicopter and the all-volunteer Sheriff’s Search and Rescue Team.
Sheriff’s Department spokesman Drew Sugars said Sunday that the 25-year-old Ventura man and three friends had set out Wednesday from the Upper Oso/Paradise Road area, about 10 miles north of Santa Barbara. The group was 12-15 miles into a trek in the Mission Pine Basin area when the man became separated from the group around midday Friday, he said.
When the man failed to appear Saturday morning, Sugars said, the three other backpackers hiked out and called 9-1-1 to report him missing.
The Search and Rescue Team and the Sheriff’s Aviation Unit were deployed around 5:30 p.m. Saturday, Sugars said.
Just before 7 p.m. Saturday, the crew of sheriff’s Copter One located the missing hiker near the trail between Upper Oso and Mission Pine Basin, Sugars said. The helicopter landed to pick him up, then transported him Upper Oso Campground, where a Search and Rescue unit was waiting.
Sugars said the man was dehydrated and exhausted, and he was treated at the scene by a crew from American Medical Response. The hiker’s identity was not released.

According to Sheriff’s Department spokesman Drew Sugars on Sunday, the man and three friends had begun their trek last Wednesday from the Upper Oso/Paradise Road area, approximately ten miles north of Santa Barbara. By Friday around midday, while the group was 12 to 15 miles into the Mission Pine Basin area, the individual became lost.

When the missing backpacker did not appear by Saturday morning, his companions hiked out and called 9-1-1 to report his disappearance. The Search and Rescue Team and the Sheriff’s Aviation Unit were deployed around 5:30 p.m. that same day. Shortly before 7 p.m., the crew of Sheriff’s Copter One located the hiker near the trail between Upper Oso and Mission Pine Basin. After landing to retrieve him, the helicopter transported him to Upper Oso Campground, where a Search and Rescue unit awaited.

Sugars reported the man was found dehydrated and exhausted. He received treatment at the scene from an American Medical Response crew. The hiker’s identity was not released.

Public invited to review public school instructional materials proposed for 2018
The state Department of Education is inviting the public to review instructional materials that are being proposed for use in South Carolina’s public schools.
The virtual public review includes three programs that school districts have requested be evaluated for possible state adoption. In January and February 2018, the recommendations for these materials will be submitted to the state Board of Education by the board’s appointed Instructional Materials Review Panel.
The three district-requested programs include:
Chinese Language Arts and Literacy Immersion Program, K-8; Publisher: Better Chinese; Program: Better Immersion Classroom Set, Levels S and 1-8;
French, 6-12; Publisher: Houghton Mifflin Harcourt; Program: Died Dit!;
Spanish, 6-12; Publisher, National Geographic and Engage Learning; Program: Exploremos!
The public will have digital access to the three programs from Dec. 11 through Jan. 9, 2018. The publisher-provided links to the materials and the link to the form to submit public commitments are posted online at goo.gl/d6NCo3.

The loss of forests in Africa in the past century is substantially less than previously estimated, an analysis of historical records and paleontology evidence by Yale researchers shows.
Previous estimates put deforestation at 35% to 55% on the continent since 1900. The new analysis estimates closed-canopy forests have shrunk by 21.7%, according to findings published Dec. 11 in the journal Nature Ecology and Evolution. However, research also shows that some West and East African forests have been reduced between 80% and 90%.
Earlier surveys incorrectly labelled ancient savannas as newly deforested regions, said A. Carla Staver, assistant professor of ecology and evolutionary biology and senior author of the study.
The new analysis should help focus conservation efforts in Africa, she said.
"There is a global effort to increase the number of trees that can trap carbon," Staver said. "In Africa, it would make the most sense to focus these efforts in areas that have truly been deforested rather than in areas which have long been savannas."
Staver and former Yale postdoc Julie C. Aleman, now at the University of Montreal, used traditional sources such as early 20th-century European maps to estimate the extent of African forests in 1900. But the team also cross-checked the documents with paleontological records -- including pollen, leaf parts known as phytoliths, and charcoal preserved in lake sediment and soil -- to reconstruct the historical ecology of tropical regions of Africa.
The single greatest contributor to continental deforestation was conversion of forests in West African countries including Ghana and Sierra Leone. However, the team also found that forests had actually expanded in Central African countries such as the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Central African Republic.
"As conservationists, it is easy to look at this study as good news -- that deforestation isn't as bad as we thought," Staver said. "The bad news is that central African forests have been spared because violent conflicts have prevented economic development, at the costs of human lives and livelihoods."
###
Aleman is lead author of the study and Yale's Mart Jarzyna is a co-author.
The research was funded by the National Science Foundation, the Seessel Fund, and the Yale Climate and Energy Institute.

A recent analysis by Yale researchers, drawing upon historical records and paleontological evidence, reveals that Africa’s forest loss over the past century is significantly lower than earlier figures suggested. Published December 11 in *Nature Ecology and Evolution*, the study concludes that closed-canopy forests have diminished by 21.7% since 1900. This contrasts sharply with prior estimates, which had placed continental deforestation between 35% and 55% during the same period. The findings do note severe reductions of 80% to 90% in certain forests of West and East Africa.

According to senior author A. Carla Staver, assistant professor of ecology and evolutionary biology, earlier assessments mistakenly categorized ancient savannas as recently deforested areas. This recalibration, she said, should help refine conservation priorities across the continent. "There is a global effort to increase the number of trees that can trap carbon," Staver noted. "In Africa, it would make the most sense to focus these efforts in areas that have truly been deforested rather than in areas which have long been savannas."

To reconstruct the historical extent of African forests around 1900, Staver and lead author Julie C. Aleman—a former Yale postdoc now at the University of Montreal—employed early 20th-century European maps alongside traditional sources. Crucially, the team cross-referenced these documents with paleontological data, such as pollen, phytoliths (microscopic plant silica parts), and charcoal preserved in lake sediments and soils. This multi-proxy approach allowed for a more accurate ecological reconstruction of Africa’s tropical regions.

The study identifies West African nations, including Ghana and Sierra Leone, as the primary contributors to continental deforestation through forest conversion. Conversely, it found that forest cover has expanded in some Central African countries, such as the Democratic Republic of the Congo and the Central African Republic. The bad news is that central African forests have been spared because violent conflicts have prevented economic development, at the costs of human lives and livelihoods."

The research, co-authored by Yale’s Mart Jarzyna, was supported by the National Science Foundation, the Seessel Fund, and the Yale Climate and Energy Institute.

…Says, I am now a born-again Christian
By Rotimi Agbana
In a new interview which graced the covers of many Nigerian newspapers on Saturday, March 17, alleged serial killer, Adeola Williams, otherwise known as Ade Lawyer admitted to lying against Prince Kazeem Eletu-Odibo and other top personalities.
According to Ade Lawyer who now claims to be a born again Christian, he also lied earlier that he worked for Prince Kazeem Eletu during the fight between him and Oba Elegushi.
Speaking on why he roped Prince Kazeem, Ade Lawyer said:
“Though I didn’t know Prince Kazeem before, I have heard his name very well and I asked for assistance from him several times through somebody who knows him but he refused to help me, and that was why I mentioned his name too. But now, I am a born-again Christian and I will always say the truth and stand by the truth.”
Prince Kazeem had earlier reacted to Ade Lawyer’s claim via a press release, where he (Kazeem) washed his hands off the allegations, stressing that the suspect has never worked for him.
Prince Kazeem disclosed that he saw him once, when he came alongside some area boys during a dispute over a land boundary, adding that it was the first and the last time he met him.
The alleged serial killer, Ade Lawyer, who was arrested for the murder of Ganiyu Ayinla, popularly known as Pinero, later affirmed Prince Kazeem’s earlier statement in his latest interview, which has been widely circulated in the media.
Reacting to Ade Lawyer’s latest confession, Prince Kazeem said:
“What else can I say which hasn’t been said in the press release I issued earlier? I don’t know him and I am very happy he has come out to say the truth. I am very grateful to God and I will continue to serve humanity irrespective of whatever they write or say about me.”
rewrite:

This admission, featured across numerous Nigerian newspaper covers, marks a significant reversal from his previous claims. Ade Lawyer, who now identifies as a born-again Christian, specifically retracted his earlier assertion that he worked for Prince Kazeem Eletu during a conflict involving Oba Elegushi.

Explaining his motives for implicating the prince, Ade Lawyer stated, “I had never met Prince Kazeem personally, though I was very familiar with his reputation. I had repeatedly sought his assistance through a mutual contact, but he declined to help me. That refusal is why I included his name in my false statements. However, as a born-again Christian now, I am committed to truthfulness and will always stand by the truth.”

This confession aligns with Prince Kazeem’s prior rebuttal, issued in an official press release. In that statement, he had categorically denied any association with the suspect, emphasizing that Ade Lawyer had never been in his employ. Prince Kazeem recounted having seen him only once, when Ade Lawyer appeared with a group of local youths during a land boundary dispute, noting that encounter was both the first and last time they met.

Ade Lawyer, arrested for the murder of Ganiyu Ayinla (known as Pinero), has now publicly corroborated the prince’s account in his recent media interview. Responding to this latest development, Prince Kazeem expressed relief, saying, “What more can I add beyond what was already stated in my earlier press release? I do not know him, and I am profoundly glad he has finally come forward with the truth. I am grateful to God and remain dedicated to serving humanity, regardless of any false narratives published about me.”

SQL Vulnerability Assessment has been available for preview on Azure SQL Database for a couple of months, and has now been released on SSMS 17.4, supporting scanning of SQL Server 2012 and up. Whether on-premises or on a VM!
SQL Vulnerability Assessment
SQL Vulnerability Assessment (VA) is your one-stop-shop to discover, track and remediate potential database vulnerabilities. It can be used as an excellent preventive security measure, providing visibility into your security state and offering actionable steps to investigate, manage and resolve security issues and enhance your database fortifications.
Vulnerability Assessment report in SSMS
Not only does VA expose some of the possible security flaws you have in your database system, it also provides remediation scripts to resolve issues within a couple of mouse clicks. In addition, you can accept specific results as your approved baseline state, and the VA scan report will be customized accordingly to expect these values.
Read the entire article here, SQL Vulnerability Assessment now available for SQL Server 2012 and up
Via the fine folks at Microsoft
rewrite:
SQL Vulnerability Assessment (VA) serves as a comprehensive solution for identifying, monitoring, and addressing potential database vulnerabilities, functioning as an effective preventive security tool. It offers clear insight into your security posture and delivers practical steps to investigate, manage, and resolve issues, thereby strengthening your database defenses. After being in preview on Azure SQL Database for several months, it is now released in SSMS 17.4, supporting scans for SQL Server 2012 and later versions, whether deployed on-premises or on a virtual machine.

Image copyright UTC Image caption University Technical College in Newhaven opened less than three years ago
A college which said it would shut after not attracting enough students has been rated "inadequate" by Ofsted.
University Technical College (UTC) in Newhaven, East Sussex, said on Monday it would stay open until July 2019 to allow current students to complete their courses.
Ofsted inspectors said many students were disappointed they had not received the education they had expected.
UTC acting principal Lisa Jepson said she accepted the report's findings.
"We are very disappointed by this outcome... and are committed to implementing the recommendations contained in their report for the students that remain with us until the UTC closes," she said.
The college opened in September 2015 for students aged 14 to 18 interested in science, technology, engineering, maths and computing.
College principal Adanma Umunna left suddenly a few weeks ago after being brought in after the first year by the Aldridge Foundation, one of the organisations involved in running UTC.
'Broken promises'
Ofsted found UTC to be inadequate in all areas, including leadership, quality of teaching, and outcomes for pupils.
Inspectors who visited the college found "too many promises had been broken too often" and teaching and leadership was ineffective.
Pupils felt "inadequately prepared" for exams, while those most able were not challenged enough.
The report also identified other problems, including frequent bullying, some of which was racial.
Ofsted visited UTC in May, in what was its first inspection.
On Monday, governors told parents, staff and students that the college had not been able "to recruit enough students to become financially stable and to deliver fully on its educational vision".
Children due to join this September will be offered alternative places.
rewrite:
A University Technical College (UTC) in Newhaven, East Sussex, has been rated "inadequate" by Ofsted, following its announcement that it will close due to insufficient student recruitment. The college, which opened in September 2015 for students aged 14 to 18 focusing on science, technology, engineering, maths, and computing, will remain open until July 2019 to allow current pupils to finish their courses. Ofsted inspectors, visiting for the first time in May, found the institution inadequate in all assessed areas: leadership, teaching quality, and pupil outcomes.

The report stated that many students felt disappointed, having not received the education they expected. Inspectors noted that "too many promises had been broken too often," with teaching and leadership deemed ineffective. Pupils reported feeling "inadequately prepared" for exams, while the most able were not sufficiently challenged. Additional issues included frequent bullying, some of which was racial.

Acting principal Lisa Jepson accepted the findings, expressing disappointment and committing to implement Ofsted's recommendations for the remaining students. The college's principal, Adanma Umunna, had left abruptly a few weeks prior; she had been brought in after the first year by the Aldridge Foundation, one of the bodies involved in running the UTC. Governors informed parents, staff, and students that the college could not "recruit enough students to become financially stable and to deliver fully on its educational vision." Children scheduled to join this September will be offered alternative placements.

Federal wildlife officials say the only wild population of endangered red wolves is unsustainable and could be wiped out within years. RALEIGH, N.C. (AP) - Federal wildlife officials say the only wild population of endangered red wolves is unsustainable and could be wiped out within years.
The prediction comes in a five-year review of the status of the species released Tuesday by the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service. The report says only about 40 wolves remain in the wild in North Carolina, down from a peak of nearly 120 a decade ago. Another 230 wolves live in captivity.
The main purpose of the report was to evaluate the wolves' endangered status, which it says should be maintained. More detailed recommendations for conservation efforts will come in a separate document.
Environmentalists contend the decline is due to neglect by federal officials who have halted releases of captive-born wolves and other actions that bolstered the wild population.
rewrite:
On April 24, 2018, the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service released a five-year review of the endangered red wolf, delivering a stark prediction: the sole wild population is unsustainable and faces potential extinction within years. According to the report, merely 40 of these wolves remain in the wild in North Carolina, a dramatic decline from a peak of approximately 120 just a decade earlier. An additional 230 wolves are maintained in captivity. The primary aim of this assessment was to evaluate the species' endangered classification, which it concludes must continue. More specific conservation strategies are slated to be outlined in a forthcoming document.

This grim forecast is linked by environmental advocates to federal neglect, citing the cessation of releasing captive-born wolves into the wild and the abandonment of other measures previously supporting the population. The report’s findings underscore a critical juncture for the species' survival.

Accompanying this news is a file photograph from June 13, 2017, taken at the Museum of Life and Science in Durham, North Carolina. The image captures a seven-week-old red wolf pup under the watchful eyes of its parents, a poignant reminder of the species' fragile future. The photograph, credited to Gerry Broome of The Associated Press, visually echoes the urgent concerns detailed in the federal review. The repeated caption with the image reinforces the central warning from wildlife officials about the precarious state of America's only wild red wolves.

Ask five basketball experts to rank the best players in the NBA and you’ll get five different lists. But, every one of those lists would include Kawhi Leonard somewhere in the top-five.
Unless you ask Penny Hardaway for his top-five, apparently. The former NBA point guard dropped a fire take over the weekend, and by “fire” I mean “god awful.” Take it away Penny…
Penny with some shots on Kawhi. pic.twitter.com/tSa7Yg93lo — ClutchPoints (@ClutchPointsApp) August 13, 2017
“He’s a good player.” Yeah, that’s an understatement. The best perimeter defender in the league can also give you 25 points a game on 48.5% shooting, but he’s merely “good.”
Leonard’s play on both ends of the court is great and all, but we’re gonna need to see him in more commercials talking to puppets before we anoint him. Same goes for Tim Duncan and Bill Russell. Sure, their 16 combined rings are impressive but have they ever appeared with Lil Yachty in a Sprite commercial? I don’t think so. #NotMySuperstars.
Seriously, though, this is a terrible take. There have always been (and will always be) low-profile superstars in sports. Barry Sanders was undoubtedly a superstar and rarely talked to the media or starred in commercials. Mike Trout is the best baseball player on the planet and is barely recognizable to casual sports fans.
In a league full of stars, Leonard manages to stand out. He doesn’t need a big social media presence or to appear in commercials to do so. His game does that for him. Leonard will never be a crossover star, but he is certainly a “superstar player,” and has been for at least two seasons now.
Now, let’s forget Hardaway ever let this nonsense come out of his mouth and just enjoy some of his highlights.
Much better.
rewrite:
If you were to request a top-five NBA player ranking from five different basketball analysts, each list would vary. However, Kawhi Leonard would consistently appear among those elite names. An exception, it seems, would be Penny Hardaway’s personal ranking. The former NBA point guard recently shared what can only be described as a truly awful take. Over the weekend, Hardaway offered his perspective, which quickly circulated online courtesy of ClutchPoints.

His assessment? “He’s a good player.” This is a profound understatement. Leonard, the league’s premier perimeter defender, also averages 25 points per game on 48.5% shooting. To label him merely “good” is absurd. His two-way dominance is undeniable, though some might humorously argue that true superstardom requires appearing in commercials with puppets. By that flawed logic, even legends like Tim Duncan and Bill Russell, with their 16 combined championships, fall short—neither shared screen time with Lil Yachty in a Sprite ad.

In all seriousness, Hardaway’s take is profoundly misguided. Sports have always featured low-profile superstars. Barry Sanders, an undeniable football icon, famously avoided the media spotlight and commercials. In baseball, Mike Trout is the planet’s best player yet remains unfamiliar to many casual fans. Within the NBA’s constellation of stars, Leonard shines brightly precisely through his performance. He doesn’t rely on a massive social media following or commercial endorsements to stand out; his game alone secures his status. While he may never become a crossover celebrity, Leonard has undoubtedly been a “superstar player” for at least the past two seasons. It’s best to dismiss Hardaway’s nonsensical comments and instead simply appreciate his own memorable highlights from his playing days.

Chief Justice Wayne Martin has given a bleak synopsis of the life of a prisoner in WA, saying those behind bars learn little more inside than “how to improve their criminal skills before being released back into the community”.
Justice Martin is retiring after more than a decade as WA’s lead jurist. His replacement is expected to be named this month.
In one of his last speeches, to an audience at the University of WA, Justice Martin admitted during his time at the head of the WA bench, little had changed in terms of outcomes for those who ended up in prison — particularly indigenous prisoners.
“To put it bluntly, for many Australian prisoners all that happens while they are in prison is they get a little older, spend time with other offenders and perhaps improve their criminal skills before being released back into the community,” he said.
In an address to launch the idea of a new-style justice centre in WA, Justice Martin had a swipe at politicians he said engaged in pre-election “law-and-order auctions”, outbidding each other in a punitive approach to crime — which in turn led to chronically overcrowded jails.
“A purely punitive response does nothing whatever to address or mitigate (crime),” Justice Martin said.
“The regular law and order auctions ... and increasingly punitive policies have caused Australia’s prison population to grow at a much faster rate than reported crime.
“That leaves me pondering aloud as to why Australia's legislators persist with increasingly punitive policies and laws. Clearly we need a new approach.”
Figures released last month by the Australian Bureau of Statistics revealed that apart from the Northern Territory, WA has the highest number of prisoners per population in the country: 342 per 100,000 adult population.
The imprisonment rate among WA’s indigenous population is by far the highest in Australia, approaching twice the national average.
Justice Martin said the incarceration percentage was now “comparable to the highest rates of disadvantage by race in any justice system in the world”.
He said if the notion of a community justice centre similar to the one running in Victoria was to take off in WA, indigenous leaders needed to be intimately involved.
“It has been said many times that those who do not learn from history are doomed to repeat it,” Justice Martin said.
rewrite:
In one of his final addresses before retiring after more than a decade as Western Australia’s lead jurist, Chief Justice Wayne Martin offered a grim assessment of prison life. Speaking at the University of WA, he stated that inmates often learn little during incarceration beyond “how to improve their criminal skills before being released back into the community.” Justice Martin, whose replacement is expected to be named this month, conceded that during his tenure at the head of the WA bench, outcomes for those entering prison—especially Indigenous prisoners—had seen little improvement.

“To put it bluntly, for many Australian prisoners all that happens while they are in prison is they get a little older, spend time with other offenders and perhaps improve their criminal skills before being released back into the community,” he remarked. His speech launched the concept of a new-style justice centre for WA, during which he also critiqued politicians for engaging in pre-election “law-and-order auctions.” He argued that this practice of outbidding each other with punitive crime policies has resulted in chronically overcrowded jails.

“A purely punitive response does nothing whatever to address or mitigate (crime),” Justice Martin asserted. “The regular law and order auctions ... and increasingly punitive policies have caused Australia’s prison population to grow at a much faster rate than reported crime.” He expressed bewilderment at the persistence of such approaches, adding, “That leaves me pondering aloud as to why Australia's legislators persist with increasingly punitive policies and laws. Clearly we need a new approach.”

Recent Australian Bureau of Statistics figures underscore the severity of the issue in WA. Excluding the Northern Territory, the state has the highest imprisonment rate in the country, with 342 prisoners per 100,000 adults. The rate among WA’s Indigenous population is by far the nation’s highest, nearing twice the national average. Justice Martin noted this incarceration percentage is now “comparable to the highest rates of disadvantage by race in any justice system in the world.”

He emphasized that for a community justice centre model, similar to one operating in Victoria, to succeed in WA, Indigenous leaders must be deeply involved in its development. Concluding with a reflective note, Justice Martin observed, “It has been said many times that those who do not learn from history are doomed to repeat it.”

Beluga whales Qila and Aurora fell ill and died at the Vancouver Aquarium in November 2016 but their DNA will contribute to efforts to preserve this species at risk. Researchers say they have collected enough DNA samples from the mother and daughter whales to sequence the complete beluga genome. That should help scientists understand how belugas are faring in an environment that is rapidly changing.
The researchers found that neither bacteria nor viruses were responsible for the fatalities, but rather they were overcome by a toxin. They have not been able to identify exactly which one.
Qila spent almost three decades at the Vancouver Aquarium before she and her daughter died from an unidentified toxin in 2016. © Jonathan Hayward/The Canadian Press/file
Genome will provide ‘many tools’
Researchers think they have mapped one of the most complete mammalian genomes and that it will provide a baseline and “many tools” to study beluga whales.
A genome is the description for the entire DNA in a living organism and determines its characteristics, inherited traits, susceptibilities and it provides a window on its evolution. Researchers say mapping “can aid in identifying conservation measures for recovery, management, and protection of a species.”
The study published in the scientific journal Genes.
rewrite:
In November 2016, the beluga whales Qila and Aurora died at the Vancouver Aquarium after falling ill. Their DNA, however, will now aid in preserving this at-risk species. According to researchers, sufficient DNA samples have been collected from this mother and daughter pair to sequence the full beluga genome. This achievement is expected to help scientists grasp how belugas are coping within a swiftly transforming environment.

Investigations revealed that the fatalities were not caused by bacteria or viruses, but by an unidentified toxin. The precise toxin remains unknown. Qila had resided at the Vancouver Aquarium for nearly thirty years prior to her death alongside her daughter in 2016.

Scientists believe they have charted one of the most comprehensive mammalian genomes to date. This genome will establish a crucial baseline and offer “many tools” for studying beluga whales. A genome encompasses the entire DNA of an organism, dictating its characteristics, inherited traits, and vulnerabilities, while also illuminating its evolutionary path. Researchers state that such mapping “can aid in identifying conservation measures for recovery, management, and protection of a species.” These findings were published in the scientific journal *Genes*.
