Middle Belt youths dissociate region from Igbo quit notice
By Nkiruka Nnorom
Middle belt youths have condemned the recent quit notice issued Igbo living in the North by Arewa Youth Consultative Forum, saying Igbo, just like other Nigerians, have the right to live in any part of the country.
The youths, acting on the platform of All Middle Belt Youth Forum, AMBYF, said in a statement by the National Leader, Mr. Aluh Moses, and the National Secretary, Mr. Andzayi Jonathan, that the entire Middle Belt region was not part of the act.
According to the statement, “we condemn, in very strong terms, the so-called Kaduna Declaration by northern youths’ coalition in its entirety, as it is a deliberate act of driving wedge between northerners and easterners.
“That the Middle Belt region is not part of the northern region. Hence, the All Middle Belt Youth Forum distances itself and the entire Middle Belt region from such obnoxious declaration.”
They urged the northern youths to retract the declaration in the interest of peace and security.
The post Middle Belt youths dissociate region from Igbo quit notice appeared first on Vanguard News.

The declaration, known as the Kaduna Declaration, was denounced as a deliberate attempt to create division between northerners and easterners. National Leader Mr. Aluh Moses and National Secretary Mr. Andzayi Jonathan emphasized that the Igbo, like all Nigerians, possess the right to reside in any part of the country.

The forum explicitly stated that the Middle Belt is not part of the northern region and, therefore, completely dissociates itself and the entire Middle Belt from what it described as an obnoxious declaration. The youths called on the northern youth coalition to retract the notice in the interest of national peace and security. Lafia – Africa’s richest man and Chairman of Dangote Group, Alhaji Aliko Dangote, has said that he would like to be known as the biggest philanthropist on the continent.
Dangote stated this on Wednesday in Lafia while disbursing N130 million micro grant to 13,000 vulnerable and less privileged women in Nasarawa State.
“I do not only want to be known as Africa’s richest man but the biggest philanthropist in Africa. I will continue to use my resources and my voice to help shape a better Nigeria and Africa as a whole,” he said.
Dangote said he started the foundation in 1993 to improve the lives of the less fortunate and make a positive difference in the growth of Nigeria.
He said the four major goals of the foundation were health and nutrition, education, economic empowerment and disaster relief.
He explained that the grant scheme was one of the components of the economic empowerment programme of the foundation.
Dangote said it was aimed at providing disadvantaged and vulnerable women in the country with a one-off unconditional N10, 000 cash transfer to boost their household income generation.
” This we believe will help their vulnerability and meet their livelihood needs,” he added .
He explained that the programme, which was launched a few years ago, was targeted at a minimum of 1,000 women in each of the 774 local government areas across the country.
“It is estimated that we would spend about N10 billion with some states with a large population getting a little bit more.
“We at Aliko Dangote foundation are happy to continue providing support to the most vulnerable and deserving members of the society across the country,” he said. (NAN)
rewrite:
During a visit to Lafia on Wednesday, Alhaji Aliko Dangote, Chairman of the Dangote Group and Africa’s wealthiest individual, expressed his desire to be recognized not merely for his riches but as the continent’s foremost philanthropist. The occasion was the disbursement of a N130 million micro grant intended for 13,000 vulnerable and less privileged women in Nasarawa State. Dangote emphasized his commitment to leveraging both his resources and his influence to foster a better future for Nigeria and Africa.

He recounted establishing the Dangote Foundation in 1993 with the core mission of enhancing the lives of the less fortunate and contributing positively to national development. The foundation’s work is structured around four primary pillars: health and nutrition, education, economic empowerment, and disaster relief. The grant initiative falls under the economic empowerment program, designed to offer a one-off, unconditional cash transfer of N10,000 to disadvantaged women. This direct support aims to strengthen household income generation, thereby reducing vulnerability and addressing basic livelihood needs.

Launched several years ago, the program targets a minimum of 1,000 women in each of Nigeria’s 774 local government areas. Dangote estimated the total commitment for this endeavor at approximately N10 billion, noting that more populous states may receive slightly larger allocations. He affirmed the foundation’s ongoing dedication to assisting the most vulnerable and deserving members of society nationwide, underscoring a philanthropic vision that seeks to reshape his legacy from one of wealth to one of widespread social impact.

A two-year-old girl died Tuesday being struck by a car in a southwest Las Vegas hospital parking lot on April 23. (Gai Phanalasy / FOX5)
A two-year-old girl died Tuesday being struck by a car in a southwest Las Vegas hospital parking lot on April 23.
Metro Police said at about 3:13 p.m. that day, the girl was walking with her family between cars at the St. Rose Pediatrics parking lot, near Buffalo Drive and the 215 freeway. A Mercedes Benz was passing through the lot and hit her.
The driver, a 35-year-old Las Vegas man, was cooperative and stayed on the scene. No impairment was involved, police said.
The girl appeared to have a severe head injury, police said, and was taken into UMC Trauma for treatment. Police said she died on May 8 at UMC.
Metro police said the girl's mother was directly supervising her daughter when the crash happened.
Doctors called the injury "horrific," police said.
A 31-year-old woman, a two year-old girl and a six-month-old girl were also in the car, but no one inside was hurt, Metro said.

The child had been walking with her family between parked cars when a Mercedes Benz passing through the lot hit her. Police reported that the driver, a 35-year-old Las Vegas man, remained at the scene and cooperated with authorities, confirming no impairment was involved.

The girl sustained what police described as a severe head injury and was transported to UMC Trauma for treatment. She ultimately died from her injuries on May 8 at the same facility. Doctors characterized the injury as "horrific." Authorities noted the girl's mother was directly supervising her daughter at the time of the crash. Inside the vehicle were a 31-year-old woman, a two-year-old girl, and a six-month-old girl, none of whom were injured. This report is copyright 2018 KVVU (KVVU Broadcasting Corporation). rewrite:
In a highly partisan environment, the House Intelligence Committee voted unanimously on Monday night to declassify a Democratic rebuttal to a controversial GOP memo on the Russia investigation, which had been released with President Trump’s blessing. This move comes amid a deepening civil war within the divided committee, where relations between Republicans and Democrats have grown so toxic that GOP members are reportedly planning to physically separate themselves from their opposition colleagues.

The Democratic memo, released over the weekend, aims to counter Republican allegations that the FBI abused surveillance rules to spy on a former Trump campaign official. Representative Adam Schiff, the top Democrat on the committee, stated on Sunday that this document demonstrates the bureau is not the "deep state" it has been portrayed as. However, President Trump swiftly shot back on Saturday, dismissing the Democrats' effort as a "very political and long response memo" concerning claims of FBI bias.

Schiff further argued that the President is reluctant to release his party's own rebuttal memo because it undermines a "claim of vindication." He also emphasized that recent indictments against 13 Russians for election meddling do not, in his view, clear the Trump administration of potential collusion, stating "of course" they do not.

Amid these intense political battles, a lighter but revealing incident surfaced. According to a Tuesday report, Russian radio hosts once pranked Schiff by falsely promising to provide compromising "naked Trump" photos, audio of which was posted by The Daily Mail. This episode underscores the bizarre and charged atmosphere surrounding the committee's work.

Democrats and Republicans have waged a public war using tweets, congressional memos, and even presidential television appearances, debating whether the FBI misused federal surveillance resources during the 2016 election. The ongoing conflict highlights the profound divisions and high stakes characterizing the investigation into Russian interference.

ANKARA (Reuters) - The deputy chairman of Turkey's main opposition Republican People's Party (CHP) said illegal acts were being carried out in favor of the government in Sunday's referendum on expanding the powers of the presidency.
"Many illegal acts are being carried out in favor of the government right now, but 'No' will win in the end," Erdal Aksunger told reporters at his party headquarters, referring to an election board decision to accept unstamped ballots.
A statement on the High Electoral Board's (YSK) website hours before polls closed said it would count ballots that had not been stamped by its officials as valid unless they could be proved fraudulent, citing a high number of complaints that YSK officials at polling stations had failed to stamp them.
With 80 percent of ballots opened, support for the constitutional changes that could hand President Tayyip Erdogan sweeping new powers stood at 53.9 percent, according to the state-run Anadolu news agency.
(Reporting by Gulsen Solaker; Writing by Ece Toksabay)
rewrite: In Sunday's referendum on expanding presidential powers, the deputy chairman of Turkey's main opposition Republican People's Party (CHP) alleged illegal acts were being conducted to benefit the government. Erdal Aksunger, speaking at party headquarters, referenced an election board decision to accept unstamped ballots, stating, "Many illegal acts are being carried out in favor of the government right now, but 'No' will win in the end." Hours before polls closed, the High Electoral Board (YSK) announced on its website that unstamped ballots would be counted as valid unless proven fraudulent, responding to numerous complaints about officials failing to stamp ballots. According to the state-run Anadolu news agency, with 80 percent of ballots opened, support for the constitutional changes granting President Tayyip Erdogan sweeping new powers stood at 53.9 percent.

The first of 10 people killed in the Toronto van attack has been identified as an employee of a US-based investment management firm, according to a report.
Anne-Marie D’Amico worked at the Canadian headquarters of Invesco located near the mile-long stretch where Alek Minassian allegedly plowed a Ryder rental van into a lunch-hour crowd, killing 10 people and injuring 15, according to the CBC.
Peter Intraligi, president of Invesco Canada, confirmed her death to the outlet.
“Our thoughts and prayers continue to be with all those impacted by this tragic event,” Intraligi said. “I can now confirm that unfortunately one of our employees has succumbed to her injuries. Out of respect for her and her family, we will not be providing any further comments.”
Minassian, 25, was due to appear in a Toronto courtroom at 10 a.m. Tuesday. Police said that charges against the suspect would be provided at that time.
The incident began about 1:30 p.m. Monday around Yonge Street and Finch Avenue and ended when Minassian was collared about a half-hour later after trying to goad police into shooting him.
“We’re all putting our pieces together to see exactly what we have,” said Toronto police Chief Mark Saunders, adding that the attack “definitely appeared deliberate.”
Garry Clement, a former Royal Canadian Mounted Police chief and, told the CBC that he thinks the cops involved “deserve to be commended because they demonstrated a lot of restraint.”
Footage shot by a bystander showed police arresting the man as he shouted: “Kill me” and pointed an object at a cop, who replied, “No, get down!”
When the suspect said, “I have a gun in my pocket,” the officer responded: “I don’t care! Get down!”
The attack shook the usually tranquil streets of Toronto, a major tourist destination. The city, which has a population of 2.8 million, recorded 61 murders last year, Reuters reported.
“This kind of tragic incident is not representative of how we live and who we are,” Mayor John Tory told reporters.
Prime Minister Justin Trudeau called the incident a “tragic and senseless attack.”
The city’s iconic CN Tower, which is normally lit up in the evening, went dark Monday evening.

Peter Intraligi, president of Invesco Canada, confirmed D’Amico’s death to the outlet. “Our thoughts and prayers continue to be with all those impacted by this tragic event,” Intraligi stated. “I can now confirm that unfortunately one of our employees has succumbed to her injuries. The violence deeply unsettled the typically tranquil streets of Toronto, a major tourist destination. Reuters reported that the city, with a population of 2.8 million, recorded 61 murders last year. Mayor John Tory addressed reporters, asserting, “This kind of tragic incident is not representative of how we live and who we are.” Prime Minister Justin Trudeau described the event as a “tragic and senseless attack.” In a symbolic gesture, the city’s iconic CN Tower, normally illuminated in the evening, remained dark on Monday night.

input: How much money do American teachers make? If your answer to that question is "not enough," you are definitely not wrong! But as recent teacher strikes have highlighted, some states are doing a much worse job of keeping teachers housed and fed than others. The folks at personal finance site HowMuch put together some maps of the average teacher salary in all 50 states using data from the Bureau of Labor Statistics, and there is way too much variation here for our liking. The maps showing middle and high school teachers' average earnings, which you can see over at HowMuch, show a similar pattern. HowMuch averaged out the median elementary, middle and high school teacher salary to calculate the top 10 states for teacher pay overall: 1. New York: $81,613 2. Alaska: $80,627 3. Connecticut: $78,567 4. California: $76,523 5. Massachusetts: $75,720 6. New Jersey: $72,460 7. Oregon: $69,643 8. Virginia: $68,707 9. Maryland: $67,173 10. Rhode Island: $67,050 [HowMuch] Not on the top ten list? West Virginia, Kentucky, Oklahoma, Colorado and Arizona, where teachers have walked out to protest low wages and insufficient benefits in recent months. If the wave of strikes continues, maybe teachers can turn all the light blue states on the above map regular blue. Or even — dare we hope? — dark blue.
rewrite:
When it comes to teacher salaries in the United States, the widespread sentiment that educators are underpaid is certainly accurate. However, recent strikes have underscored that the financial challenges teachers face vary dramatically from state to state. Using Bureau of Labor Statistics data, the personal finance site HowMuch created maps illustrating average teacher salaries across all 50 states, revealing a troubling degree of disparity.

A similar pattern emerges in maps for middle and high school teachers' average earnings, also available at HowMuch. The site compiled an overall ranking by averaging the median salaries for elementary, middle, and high school teachers, resulting in a top ten list: New York leads at $81,613, followed by Alaska ($80,627), Connecticut ($78,567), California ($76,523), Massachusetts ($75,720), New Jersey ($72,460), Oregon ($69,643), Virginia ($68,707), Maryland ($67,173), and Rhode Island ($67,050).

Noticeably absent from this top tier are states like West Virginia, Kentucky, Oklahoma, Colorado, and Arizona, where teachers have recently walked out to protest low wages and inadequate benefits. If the current wave of strikes persists, perhaps educators can shift the lighter blue states on these salary maps to a deeper blue—or, hopefully, even to the darkest shade indicating the highest pay.

There is no shortage of options.
"We have a very good understanding of the needs of our football team," Newsome said. "What we try to do is to match that with the players."
Some things to know about the Ravens' draft:
TIGHT END NEEDED
The leading receiver on the team last season was tight end Benjamin Watson, who joined the Saints as a free agent.
A replacement is sorely needed, and after failing to secure one through free agency, the Ravens will look to snag one in the draft.
"There are some pretty good ones out there. And they're of the athletic variety, pass-catching tight ends that certainly could help impact our offence," said Joe Horitz, director of college scouting.
One of Newsome's best picks was tight end Todd Heap, selected in the first round in 2001 even though the Ravens already had future Hall of Fame star Shannon Sharpe.
TRADE OR NOT?
Newsome cryptically mentioned the possibility of trading the No. 16 pick, but DeCosta likes the idea of drafting in the middle of the round.
"We're in a good spot for a lot of different reasons," DeCosta said. "I think 16 is a good spot to be in this draft. It plays well to our needs and different strategies."
VOLCANO BREWING
Coach John Harbaugh has been in the Ravens draft room since 2008, and when it comes time for Baltimore to make a pick, he just gets out of the way.
"I'll tell you, it's like a volcano, kind of. It's festering, like, 'Is this thing going to blow?' It never quite blows, but there's so much tension," Harbaugh said.
In the end, though, it's Newsome's call.
"Ozzie pulls the trigger and makes a decision," Harbaugh said, "and we all feel good about it."
HITS, MISSES AND BARGAINS
Perriman missed the entire 2015 season with a knee injury, caught 33 passes in 2016 and last season had a mere 10 catches for the league's 29th-ranked passing attack.
Newsome also struck out with safety Matt Elam at No. 32 overall in 2013. But he recently found two fourth-round gems: Defensive end Brent Urban in 2014 and offensive lineman Alex Lewis in 2016.
___
For more NFL coverage: http://www.pro32.ap.org and http://www.twitter.com/AP_NFL
By David Ginsburg, The Associated Press
rewrite:
The Ravens enter the draft with a clear plan. "We have a very good understanding of the needs of our football team," stated General Manager Ozzie Newsome. "What we try to do is to match that with the players." With numerous possibilities available, the team is poised to address several key areas.

A pressing need is at tight end. Last season's leading receiver, Benjamin Watson, departed via free agency to the Saints. Having not filled this void in free agency, the Ravens are now focused on the draft. Joe Horitz, the director of college scouting, noted, "There are some pretty good ones out there. And they're of the athletic variety, pass-catching tight ends that certainly could help impact our offence." Newsome has a history of success at this position, having selected Todd Heap in the first round in 2001 despite already having future Hall of Famer Shannon Sharpe on the roster.

Regarding their first-round position at No. 16 overall, Newsome hinted at a potential trade. However, Assistant General Manager Eric DeCosta expressed satisfaction with their spot. "We're in a good spot for a lot of different reasons," DeCosta said. "I think 16 is a good spot to be in this draft. It plays well to our needs and different strategies."

Inside the draft room, a unique tension builds. Coach John Harbaugh, who has been part of the process since 2008, described the atmosphere. "I'll tell you, it's like a volcano, kind of. It's festering, like, 'Is this thing going to blow?' It never quite blows, but there's so much tension," he said. Ultimately, the final decision rests with Newsome. "Ozzie pulls the trigger and makes a decision," Harbaugh confirmed, "and we all feel good about it."

The Ravens' draft history includes both disappointments and late-round successes. Wide receiver Breshad Perriman, a first-round pick, missed 2015 with injury and had only 10 catches last season for the league's 29th-ranked passing attack. Safety Matt Elam, selected 32nd overall in 2013, was another miss. Yet Newsome has also uncovered bargains, such as defensive end Brent Urban (2014) and offensive lineman Alex Lewis (2016), both found in the fourth round.

Over time, however, Edmonton’s location — and, in particular, the lack of direct flights from New York — came to feel like a plus, rather than a minus.
Advertisement Continue reading the main story
“There was something attractive about doing it in a place where there wouldn’t be a whole set of eyes seeing the work and judging it before it’s fully baked,” Ms. Chavkin, who had never been to Edmonton and had never heard of Citadel, said.
Then there was the money.
The American dollar stretches further in Canada. And Citadel was not asking for much — the theater agreed to spend what it usually spends to stage a musical (about $600,000 Canadian) and also agreed not to seek a royalty from future productions (nonprofits that help develop commercial shows often get a percentage of Broadway profits).
The commercial producers would pay the rest of the costs, and bring their own sound and lighting equipment, a revolving stage, and significant set elements to upgrade what they would find at Citadel.
Photo
“There was no question it was financially in our interest to go to Canada,” said Ms. Isaacs, who is producing the show along with Mr. Kirdahy, Dale Franzen, and Hunter Arnold.
During just three weeks of rehearsal and four previews, Ms. Chavkin restaged the show several times over, with new cast members, including Reeve Carney (“Spider-Man: Turn Off the Dark”), in three of the five main roles. At first, a rail line bisected the stage; the creative team scrapped that design after a single performance. There were several experiments with how best to deploy characters added for the Edmonton production in an effort to bring to life, as it were, those toiling away in hell.
“We’re trying to walk this line between maintaining the metaphorical and poetic world, and also trying to deliver a satisfying story,” Ms. Mitchell said. “The only way we know where it comfortably wants to sit is by going too far in one direction or another.”
The Citadel says that if it worked on a Broadway-aimed show again, it would dedicate a staffer to managing relations with the commercial producers, because immigration and budget issues proved more time-consuming than anticipated.
rewrite:
Edmonton’s relative isolation, especially its lack of direct flights from New York, gradually came to be viewed as an advantage rather than a drawback. As director Rachel Chavkin, who was unfamiliar with both the city and the Citadel Theatre prior to this project, noted, there was an appeal in developing the work in a setting removed from the immediate scrutiny and judgment of a major theatrical center before it was fully realized. Financial considerations also played a significant role. The favorable exchange rate meant the American dollar went further in Canada. Moreover, the Citadel’s terms were accommodating: the theater committed only its standard musical production budget, approximately $600,000 Canadian, and waived any future royalty claims from subsequent productions, a departure from the common practice where nonprofit incubators receive a share of Broadway profits.

The remaining expenses were covered by the commercial producers, who also supplied their own enhanced sound and lighting equipment, a revolving stage, and major set pieces to augment the Citadel’s existing resources. Producer Isaacs, collaborating with Kirdahy, Dale Franzen, and Hunter Arnold, stated unequivocally that the Canadian venture made clear financial sense for their side. The Edmonton residency became a period of intensive revision. Over a compact schedule of three weeks of rehearsal and four previews, Chavkin repeatedly restaged the production. This process incorporated new cast members, such as Reeve Carney in one of the lead roles, and involved considerable experimentation. An initial staging concept featuring a rail line dividing the stage was abandoned after just one performance. The creative team also tested various ways to effectively integrate additional characters, unique to this production, to vividly portray the figures laboring in a hellish setting.

Writer and composer Anaïs Mitchell described the ongoing challenge of balancing the show’s metaphorical and poetic essence with the demands of coherent storytelling, explaining that finding the right equilibrium often required pushing boundaries to extremes. Reflecting on the experience, the Citatel noted that any future collaboration on a Broadway-bound show would involve assigning a dedicated staff member to oversee relations with commercial producers. This adjustment was prompted by the unforeseen time demands of navigating immigration logistics and budget coordination, which proved more consuming than initially expected.

An employee stands outside a Lowe's home improvement chain in Austin, Texas, U.S., February 27, 2017. REUTERS/Mohammad Khursheed
NEW YORK Shares of home improvement retailer Lowe's Companies Inc (LOW.N) could rise by 20 percent or more, helped by better projected earnings growth this year and greater room for margin improvement, Barron's said on Sunday.
Companies such as Lowe's and Home Depot Inc (HD.N) are uniquely positioned due to their strong outlook, as a healthy economy and improving real estate markets in most of the United States encourages homeowners to undertake renovation, Barron's said.
These companies are also "Amazon proof", the report said, noting that home improvement was low on the list of categories the retailer is expected to penetrate.
U.S. retail heavyweights including Target Corp (TGT.N), Wal-Mart Stores Inc (WMT.N) and Kroger Co (KR.N) have been locked in a fierce battle against Amazon Inc (AMZN.O).
While both Home Depot and Lowe's are poised for growth, Lowe's could be more attractive now, due in part to its lower price-to-earnings ratio, the report said.
Lowe's shares trade at $82, or about 18 times projected earnings of $4.63 per share for year ending January 2018, while Home Depot trades at $147, or 20.4 times estimated earnings of $7.19 per share in its current year, Barron's said.
Lowe's same-store sales performance has lagged Home Depot's the past several quarters, mainly due to its focus on do-it-yourself customers who spend less on big-ticket items than professionals.
However, the retailer is taking steps to boost per-store revenue, which would help narrow the valuation gap, Barron's said.
Lowe's offers investors exposure to one of retail's strongest sectors, the potential for 15 percent annual earnings growth and a "shareholder friendly" management, according to the report.
(Reporting by Devika Krishna Kumar in New York; Editing by Meredith Mazzilli)
rewrite:
On Sunday, Barron's reported that shares of Lowe's Companies Inc (LOW.N) possess potential for a rise of 20 percent or more. This outlook is supported by better projected earnings growth for the year and significant room for margin improvement. The home improvement sector, featuring companies like Lowe's and Home Depot Inc (HD.N), is seen as uniquely positioned for strength. A healthy U.S. economy and improving real estate markets in most regions are encouraging homeowners to invest in renovations, contributing to a robust industry outlook.

Notably, the report described these home improvement retailers as "Amazon proof," highlighting that this category is low on the list of sectors Amazon Inc (AMZN.O) is expected to penetrate deeply. This stands in contrast to other U.S. retail heavyweights, such as Target Corp (TGT.N), Wal-Mart Stores Inc (WMT.N), and Kroger Co (KR.N), which are locked in a fierce battle with the online giant.

While both major home improvement chains are poised for growth, Barron's suggested Lowe's could currently be more attractive to investors. This is partly due to its lower price-to-earnings ratio. Lowe's shares trade at $82, or about 18 times the projected earnings of $4.63 per share for the year ending January 2018. In comparison, Home Depot trades at $147, or 20.4 times its current year's estimated earnings of $7.19 per share.

Although Lowe's same-store sales have lagged behind Home Depot's in recent quarters—primarily because its focus on do-it-yourself customers, who spend less on big-ticket items than professional contractors—the company is taking steps to boost per-store revenue. These measures are expected to help narrow the valuation gap. According to the report, Lowe's offers investors exposure to one of retail's strongest sectors, the potential for 15 percent annual earnings growth, and a management team deemed "shareholder friendly." The original article was reported by Devika Krishna Kumar in New York and edited by Meredith Mazzilli. A related photo from February 27, 2017, showed an employee outside a Lowe's in Austin, Texas.

A proposed Snowboard and Freeski Big Air World Cup competition due to take place in Düsseldorf next season has been postponed for a year due to a scheduling conflict.
The event had been scheduled to be held on a temporary ramp in the Espirit Arena in January, the same venue which hosted the World Table Tennis Championships last year.
Organisers have determined, however, that there will be "insufficient time to realise the construction of the competition ramp" in the 54,000 capacity venue due to other events also taking place there.
"Because of this, the decision was made to postpone the event from the 2018/19 season until the 2019/20 World Cup season, where the safety of the athletes can remain paramount and the true vision for the competition can be fully realised," said the International Ski Federation (FIS).
"At this time the proposed schedule for the Düsseldorf Snowboard and Freeski big air World Cup will see the competition held from January 2 to 4, 2020."
The Big Air event in Düsseldorf had been due to take place in the Espirit Arena ©SOP Architekten
The Big Air World Cup season is due to begin in Cardrona in New Zealand in September and continue with events in Milan, Beijing, Canyons in United States, Quebec and Oslo.
"While the cancellation of this season’s Dusseldorf event is disappointing for all parties involved, excitement for the 2020 event is high as the FIS snowboard and freeski tours look forward to bringing World Cup big air action to one of the great cities of Europe," FIS added.
"With Düsseldorf 54,000 seat Espirit Arena - home to the Fortuna [football team who recently earned promotion to the Bundesliga for the 2018/19 season] - lined up to host the competition, the Düsseldorf snowboard and freeski big air competitions are set to be season highlights in January 2020."
rewrite:
Due to a scheduling conflict, a planned Snowboard and Freeski Big Air World Cup in Düsseldorf has been postponed by one year. The competition was originally slated for the upcoming season inside the city’s Espirit Arena on a temporary ramp, the same venue that held the World Table Tennis Championships last year. Organizers concluded there is "insufficient time to realise the construction of the competition ramp" within the 54,000-seat arena because of other events booked at the location. Consequently, the International Ski Federation (FIS) announced the event will move from the 2018/19 season to the 2019/20 World Cup season. This shift will ensure "the safety of the athletes can remain paramount and the true vision for the competition can be fully realised."

The rescheduled Düsseldorf Big Air World Cup is now proposed for January 2 to 4, 2020. The broader Big Air World Cup season will still launch as planned in Cardrona, New Zealand, this September, with subsequent stops in Milan, Beijing, Canyons in the United States, Quebec, and Oslo. Although disappointing for all involved this season, anticipation is building for the 2020 event. The FIS expressed high excitement about bringing World Cup big air to "one of the great cities of Europe."

The venue itself adds to the event’s promise: the Espirit Arena is a 54,000-seat stadium, home to the Fortuna football team, which recently earned promotion to the Bundesliga for the 2018/19 season. With this impressive facility set to host, the Düsseldorf snowboard and freeski big air competitions are positioned as major highlights for January 2020.

MIAMI (WFLA) – CarePlus Health Plans is notifying customers after a privacy breach that occurred on Jan. 17.
The breach occurred due to a series of programming and printing errors, resulting in Explanation of Benefits letters being mailed to the incorrect CarePlus member.
The EOBs impacted with the errors were mailed out on Jan. 9 and Jan. 16. Roughly 11,200 members’ information as sent to another member.
Personal financial information and Social Security numbers were not contained in the letters.
The information disclosed included:
Member name
CarePlus identification number and plan name
Date(s) of service(s)
Provider of service
Services provided
CarePlus has no information that any data has been inappropriately used.
Anyone who notices any changes in their EOB statement, SmartSummary or medical records that are unfamiliar to them, or customers who have any questions, should contact CarePlus at 1-800-794-5907, from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m.

rewrite: On January 17, a privacy breach took place at CarePlus Health Plans, prompting the company to notify its customers. Recently it was reported that the Penn State Outing Club, Nittany Grotto Caving Club and Scuba Club lost their official University recognition. A "risk assessment" deemed the clubs too risky. What a shame! The Caving Club has sponsored regular trips for 70 years; the Outing Club is nearly 100 years old.
What has changed over the past 100 years that would cause Penn State University to take such a drastic step? Lawsuits, lawyers, and a whole lot of money.
According to student leaders of these organizations, losing campus recognition means a club will no longer be covered under the university's $1 million liability insurance policy. I will put it more bluntly: It is too risky for Penn State to continue insuring these clubs because of the constant threat of lawsuits. That pot of a million bucks is just too attractive to plaintiffs' attorneys. The propensity to sue in our overly litigious society puts Penn State and any large organization with deep pockets right in the cross hairs of lawyers.
While some might blame Penn State for being too cautious, the university is not really to blame here. It must make these decisions mindful that attorneys are always looking for the chance to strike. And it's not just "dear old State." Thanks to abusive lawsuits, entire industries have disappeared in Pennsylvania and the cost of goods and services continue to rise as the explosive costs of litigation are factored in. Penn State and its students are just the most recent victims.
It begs the question: Where will the plaintiffs' attorneys strike next? Perhaps the table tennis club?
Curt Schroder
Executive director, Pennsylvania Coalition for Civil Justice Reform
Hatrisburg
rewrite:
The recent loss of official university recognition for the Penn State Outing Club, Nittany Grotto Caving Club, and Scuba Club marks a significant shift. This decision, stemming from a formal risk assessment, deems these long-standing groups too hazardous. It is a regrettable outcome, particularly given the Caving Club’s 70-year history of sponsored trips and the Outing Club’s nearly century-long presence.

So what has transformed over the past hundred years to prompt such a drastic measure by Penn State University? The answer lies in a landscape dominated by lawsuits, lawyers, and substantial financial stakes. Student leaders clarify that without campus recognition, these clubs forfeit coverage under the university’s $1 million liability insurance policy. To state it plainly, the persistent threat of litigation makes it too risky for Penn State to continue providing this insurance. That million-dollar reserve proves an irresistible target for plaintiffs’ attorneys. In our excessively litigious society, this tendency to sue places Penn State—and any well-resourced institution—directly in the legal crosshairs.

Though some may criticize the university for excessive caution, Penn State itself is not the true culprit. The administration must operate under the constant reality that attorneys are poised to seize any opportunity. This issue extends far beyond the campus. Abusive lawsuits have led to the disappearance of entire industries within Pennsylvania, while the soaring costs of litigation drive up prices for goods and services. Penn State and its students are merely the latest casualties in this broader trend.

This situation raises a pressing question: where will plaintiffs’ lawyers focus next? Could even the table tennis club become a target?

Curt Schroder
Executive director, Pennsylvania Coalition for Civil Justice Reform
Harrisburg

MELBOURNE Australia pace spearhead Mitchell Starc and batsman Chris Lynn have been named as part of a formidable squad for next month's Champions Trophy in England and Wales despite nursing injuries.
Starc was forced to pull out midway through the India tour last month with a fractured foot while Lynn has been sidelined with a shoulder injury during the Indian Premier League.
Both are expected to be fit for Australia's opener on June 2 against New Zealand.
"Our medical staff will continue to monitor Mitchell and Chris’s recovery from their respective injuries but we are hopeful they will be fit in time for the team’s departure on May 18,” selector Trevor Hohns said in a media release.
James Faulkner, man-of-the-match in the 2015 World Cup final against New Zealand, has been omitted from the 15-man squad named on Thursday, with selectors opting for all-rounders Moises Henriques, Glenn Maxwell and Marcus Stoinis.
Young fast bowler Pat Cummins and James Pattinson, on the comeback trail after suffering stress fractures in his back, were included in an imposing pace battery along with Josh Hazlewood and John Hastings.
"Both James and John have made very good returns from injury and are bowling well for their respective teams in the English county competition as well as both contributing well with the bat," Hohns said.
"When you also add Mitchell Starc, Josh Hazlewood and Pat Cummins to the fast bowling artillery it becomes a very exciting proposition for Australian cricket."
Legspinner Adam Zampa is the sole specialist spinner in the squad, while batsmen Usman Khawaja, George Bailey and Peter Handscomb have missed out.
World champions Australia, who lost their top ranking to South Africa earlier this year, will bid for their third win in the quadrennial one-day international tournament after back-to-back triumphs in 2006 and 2009.
Squad:
Steve Smith (captain), David Warner, Pat Cummins, Aaron Finch, John Hastings, Josh Hazlewood, Travis Head, Moises Henriques, Chris Lynn, Glenn Maxwell, James Pattinson, Mitchell Starc, Marcus Stoinis, Matthew Wade, Adam Zampa
(Reporting by Ian Ransom; Editing by Amlan Chakraborty/Peter Rutherford)
rewrite:
Despite currently recovering from injuries, Australian pace bowler Mitchell Starc and batsman Chris Lynn have been selected for a powerful squad to compete in next month's Champions Trophy in England and Wales. Starc sustained a fractured foot, which led to his withdrawal during last month's tour of India, while Lynn has been recovering from a shoulder injury suffered in the Indian Premier League. Selectors are optimistic both players will be fit for Australia's first match against New Zealand on June 2. Trevor Hohns, a national selector, stated that medical staff are monitoring their progress and expressed hope for their readiness by the team's departure date of May 18.

The 15-member squad, announced on Thursday, sees the omission of James Faulkner, who was man-of-the-match in the 2015 World Cup final. Instead, the selectors have chosen all-rounders Moises Henriques, Glenn Maxwell, and Marcus Stoinis. The fast bowling unit appears particularly strong, featuring Pat Cummins and the returning James Pattinson, who has recovered from stress fractures in his back. They join Josh Hazlewood and John Hastings, with Hohns noting that both Pattinson and Hastings have returned effectively from injury and are performing well with bat and ball in English county cricket. Hohns added that combining them with Starc, Hazlewood, and Cummins creates an exciting prospect for the team.

Adam Zampa is included as the squad's only specialist legspinner. Notable absences among the batsmen are Usman Khawaja, George Bailey, and Peter Handscomb. Australia, the current world champions who recently ceded the top ODI ranking to South Africa, will aim to secure their third Champions Trophy title, having previously won the tournament in 2006 and 2009.

The full squad is: Steve Smith (captain), David Warner, Pat Cummins, Aaron Finch, John Hastings, Josh Hazlewood, Travis Head, Moises Henriques, Chris Lynn, Glenn Maxwell, James Pattinson, Mitchell Starc, Marcus Stoinis, Matthew Wade, and Adam Zampa.

MORRIS, Minn. — A 94-year-old Minnesota man whose wife died after battling cancer built a swimming pool in his backyard for children in his neighborhood.
Keith Davison’s wife of 66 years died last year, KARE 11 reports.
“You just can’t imagine what it’s like,” he said. “You cry a lot. That’s just the way it is because she’s not here.”
Davison then decided to do something different to fill his time.
In the spring, the retired judge had an in-ground pool built. In July, the pool, which is 32 feet long and 9 feet deep, opened — and kids from all over the neighborhood came to swim.
“I knew they’d come,” Davison said.
Davison, who has three adult children but no grandchildren, is usually seen sitting in a chair next to the pool, watching the kids swimming, laughing and having fun.
“I’m not sitting by myself looking at the walls,” Davison said. “What else would you think of doing where you could have a whole bunch of kids over every afternoon?”
rewrite:
In Morris, Minnesota, a retired judge named Keith Davison, 94, recently built a large in-ground swimming pool in his backyard. This project began after the death of his wife of 66 years following a battle with cancer. "You just can’t imagine what it’s like," Davison said of his loss. "You cry a lot. That’s just the way it is because she’s not here."

Seeking a new way to fill his time and his quiet home, he had the 32-foot-long, 9-foot-deep pool constructed this past spring. By July, it was open, immediately drawing children from throughout the neighborhood. "I knew they’d come," he remarked.

Now, Davison, who has three adult children but no grandchildren of his own, often sits in a chair beside the pool. He watches the children swim, laugh, and enjoy themselves. "I’m not sitting by myself looking at the walls," he explained. "What else would you think of doing where you could have a whole bunch of kids over every afternoon?"

By Liana B. Baker and Olivia Oran
April 12 Morgan Stanley's chief compliance officer Billy Fenrich is leaving the firm just over a year after being named to the position.
Fenrich will be replaced by Raul Yanes, according to an internal Morgan Stanley memo reviewed by Reuters, which was confirmed by a firm spokesman.
Fenrich is joining quantitative hedge fund AQR Capital Management as its chief legal officer, according to an AQR spokeswoman.
Yanes was most recently a litigation partner at the law firm Davis Polk & Wardwell and had also served in a number of senior positions under president George W. Bush, including staff secretary and assistant to the president and senior counselor to the attorney general.
Fenrich joined Morgan Stanley's legal department in 2014 from hedge fund PointState Capital. He was named chief compliance officer in 2016, replacing longtime compliance chief Stuart Breslow. He had also worked at Davis Polk.
Compliance officers have become critical figures on Wall Street since the financial crisis, helping to ensure that bankers and traders stay out of trouble and avoid massive fines. (Reporting by Liana Baker and Olivia Oran in New York; Editing by Tom Brown)

HOLLYWOOD stars including Ellen DeGeneres, Paris Hilton, and Chelsea Handler were forced to evacuate their homes as the deadly fire in California continues to burn.
President Donald Trump has declared a state of emergency and ordered federal agencies to help with rescue efforts.
White House spokeswoman Lindsay Walters said Agriculture Secretary Sonny Perdue briefed Trump and Vice President Mike Pence on a wildfire prevention roundtable today.
Walters said the White House “continues to closely monitor the situation” and is urging “anyone ordered to evacuate during a wildfire, do so immediately and listen to your local and state officials”.
Camera Icon Firefighters monitor a blaze beside Highway 33 near Ojai. Picture: AFP Picture: AFP Camera Icon Firefighters comb through smouldering ash in the remains of dozens of homes destroyed by the Lilac Fire in San Diego. Picture: AFP Picture: AFP
She also said the White House “extends its thoughts and prayers” to everyone affected by the fires that have been tearing through Southern California.
Authorities today issued new alerts about unhealthy air from smoke and ash sent up by the growing wildfire.
Celebrities including former Glee star Lea Michele, talk show host DeGeneres, along with Hilton and Kylie Jenner were forced to flee their homes and, in Jenner’s case, her Kylie Cosmetics headquarters.
Richard Sanchez, a manager at Jeannine’s American Bakery restaurant in the foothill enclave of Montecito, said customers were wearing masks.
Camera Icon Flames erupt on mountainsides in the Los Padres national forest north of Ojai. Picture: AFP Picture: AFP
He said smoke was so thick that visibility was down to a few metres and a layer of ash was coating the streets.
Regulators were warning resident in parts of Santa Barbara, Ventura and Los Angeles counties to stay indoors, avoid vigorous outdoor activities and not do anything to stir up ash.
Even residents of Montecito and neighbouring Carpinteria who weren’t under evacuation orders opted to leave because of the thick blanket of smoke.
rewrite:
As the deadly California wildfires continue to rage, numerous Hollywood celebrities have been compelled to evacuate their residences. Among those forced to flee are Ellen DeGeneres, Paris Hilton, Chelsea Handler, former *Glee* star Lea Michele, and Kylie Jenner, who also left her Kylie Cosmetics headquarters. In response to the escalating crisis, President Donald Trump has declared a state of emergency, directing federal agencies to assist in rescue operations.

White House spokeswoman Lindsay Walters stated that Agriculture Secretary Sonny Perdue briefed both President Trump and Vice President Mike Pence during a wildfire prevention roundtable. Walters emphasized that the White House “continues to closely monitor the situation” and urgently advised that “anyone ordered to evacuate during a wildfire, do so immediately and listen to your local and state officials.” She added that the administration “extends its thoughts and prayers” to all individuals impacted by the fires tearing through Southern California.

Authorities have issued new alerts concerning unhealthy air quality resulting from smoke and ash propelled by the expanding blazes. In the foothill enclave of Montecito, Richard Sanchez, a manager at Jeannine’s American Bakery restaurant, observed customers wearing masks. He described smoke so dense that visibility was reduced to just a few meters, with a layer of ash coating the streets. Regulators warned residents in portions of Santa Barbara, Ventura, and Los Angeles counties to remain indoors, avoid strenuous outdoor activities, and refrain from any actions that could stir up ash.

Even residents of Montecito and the neighboring Carpinteria area, who were not under formal evacuation orders, chose to depart due to the thick, pervasive smoke. Meanwhile, firefighters remain engaged in intense efforts, monitoring blazes beside Highway 33 near Ojai and combing through smoldering ash in the remnants of dozens of homes destroyed by the Lilac Fire in San Diego. Flames continue to erupt on mountainsides in the Los Padres National Forest north of Ojai.

A World War One grave in France marked as that of an unknown soldier has been identified as the resting place of an army officer from Scotland.
The headstone at Jonchery-Sur-Vesle, near Reims, was dedicated only to "a major" of the Royal Engineers.
Detective work by David Tattersfield, of the Western Front Association, identified the major to be an Alexander Soutar, a minister's son.
Maj Soutar was born in Cullen and grew up in Glasgow and Thurso.
He fought at the Somme in 1916 and Passchendale in 1917, before being shot and killed by a sniper on 28 May 1918 while helping to defend the village of Hermonville, near Jonchery-Sur-Vesle, from an attack by German soldiers.
One hundred years after his death, Maj Soutar's descendants have gathered at the Commonwealth War Graves Commission Cemetery where he lies to honour him.
A new headstone with his name has been erected.
rewrite: In a cemetery near Reims, France, a World War One grave long marked for an unknown soldier has now been identified. It belongs to Major Alexander Soutar of the Royal Engineers, a Scottish army officer. The detective work of David Tattersfield from the Western Front Association made this discovery possible. Maj Soutar, son of a minister, was born in Cullen and raised in Glasgow and Thurso. His wartime service included the battles of the Somme in 1916 and Passchendaele in 1917. He was ultimately shot by a sniper on May 28, 1918, while helping defend the village of Hermonville near the cemetery. One century after his death, his descendants gathered at the Commonwealth War Graves Commission site to honour him, where a new headstone bearing his name has been erected.

ROCHESTER, Mich. — Tai Odiase had 19 points, on 8-for-8 shooting, and three blocks, Godwin Boahen hit four 3-pointers and finished with 16 points and Illinois-Chicago beat Oakland 79-73 on Friday night for its fifth win in a row.
Marcus Ottey added 15 points and Tarkus Ferguson had 13 points, nine rebounds and seven assists for UIC (13-11, 8-3 Horizon League). The Flames have eight conference wins for the first time since finishing the 2007-08 season 9-9 in Horizon League play.
Odiase had a dunk and two layups during a 6-2 spurt that made it 17-14 and UIC led the rest of the way. Ferguson converted a 3-point play to spark a 10-2 run that pushed the lead to 11 points before Boahen's 3-pointer made it 40-30 at the break. Nick Daniels hit a 3 that pulled Oakland (14-10, 6-5) within two points with two minutes to play, but Ottey made two free throws and Odiase hit a jumper to make it 76-69 and UIC made 4 of 6 free throws in the final 32 seconds to seal it.
Martez Walker had 21 points and Jalen Hayes scored 15 for Oakland. Kendrick Nunn added 20, but shot 3 of 22 from the field, including 1 of 10 from 3-point range.
rewrite:
On Friday night, Illinois-Chicago extended its winning streak to five games by defeating Oakland 79-73 in Rochester, Mich. Tai Odiase led the Flames with a perfect 8-for-8 shooting performance, contributing 19 points and three blocks. Godwin Boahen added 16 points, including four three-pointers. Marcus Ottey scored 15 points, while Tarkus Ferguson recorded 13 points, nine rebounds, and seven assists for UIC, which improved to 13-11 overall and 8-3 in Horizon League play. This marks the first time since the 2007-08 season, when they finished 9-9 in conference play, that the Flames have achieved eight league wins.

UIC took control early after a 6-2 run, featuring a dunk and two layups from Odiase, gave them a 17-14 lead, which they maintained throughout. A three-point play by Ferguson sparked a 10-2 surge, pushing the advantage to 11 points, and Boahen’s three-pointer sent UIC into halftime ahead 40-30. Oakland (14-10, 6-5) narrowed the gap to two points with two minutes remaining after a three-pointer from Nick Daniels. However, Ottey made two free throws and Odiase hit a key jumper to extend the lead to 76-69. The Flames sealed the victory by making four of six free throws in the final 32 seconds.

For Oakland, Martez Walker scored 21 points and Jalen Hayes added 15. Kendrick Nunn contributed 20 points but struggled from the field, shooting only 3 of 22, including 1 of 10 from beyond the arc.

The Center for Law and Social Justice at Medgar Evers College is a winner of the Brooklyn Community Foundation’s Annual Spark Prize, which recognizes exceptional nonprofits rooted in Brooklyn that advances racial and social justice. The center will receive $100,000 in general operating support from the foundation.
CLSJ is one of five organizations receiving the prestigious Spark Prize, along with the Cave Canem Foundation, Exalt Youth, GRIOT Circle and the Red Hook Initiative. The organizations, each receiving $100,000, were selected from a pool of over 130 applicants by a 30-member committee of Brooklyn leaders in business, civics and philanthropy. All will be honored February 8 at a celebration breakfast hosted by actress and comedian Ana Gasteyer that includes a tribute to Hildy J. Simmons, a philanthropic leader and longtime Brooklyn Community Foundation board member.
“We are absolutely thrilled to be selected as a winner of the Spark Prize Award,” said Esmeralda Simmons, Esq., founder and executive director of CLSJ. “It is our mission to advocate for and assist African descendant and disenfranchised communities on racial justice issues such as voter rights, educational inequity, police violence, as well as tackling issues that impact women of color, and this award will help us further that mission.”
The Brooklyn Community Foundation is dedicated to Brooklyn’s charitable community and partners with donors and community leaders to bolster nonprofits, strengthen neighborhoods and increase opportunities for youth. Simmons expressed gratitude to Foundation President and CEO Cecilia Clarke for aiding social justice initiatives in Brooklyn. She also thanked the Brooklyn community for their continued support.
Medgar Evers College’s renowned Center for Law and Social Justice provides advocacy, training and expert services in a personal manner. CLSJ conducts research and initiates advocacy projects and litigation on behalf of community organizations and groups that promote human, national and international understanding.
The Spark Prize, sponsored by TD Bank with support from National Grid, is presented by the Brooklyn Community Foundation in partnership with the Office of the Brooklyn Borough President and the Brooklyn Chamber of Commerce.

FORD COUNTY – One person was injured in a 3-vehicle accident just after 4p.m. on Tuesday in Ford County.
The Kansas Highway Patrol reported a 2016 Dodge Ram pickup driven by Jessee Stickell, 51, Pottsville, PA., was northbound on U.S. 56 just south of U.S. 400.
As the pickup approached the intersection at Lariat Way, a 2001 Cadillac DeVille driven by Jose G. Soto-Gonzalez, 30, Dodge City, attempted to cross U.S. 56 from Lariat Way.
The Dodge collided with the Cadillac and rolled into the northeast ditch. The Cadillac spun around and hit a USD 443 school bus driven by Wade S. Hampton, 64, Dodge City, that was stopped on Lariat Way headed west bound on U.S. 56.
Stickel was transported to Western Plains Medical Center.
Soto-Gonzalez, Hampton and 9 children on the school bus were not injured.
The drivers were properly restrained at the time of the accident, according to the KHP.
rewrite: A three-vehicle accident in Ford County on Tuesday shortly after 4 p.m. resulted in one injury. According to the Kansas Highway Patrol, a 2016 Dodge Ram pickup, driven by 51-year-old Jessee Stickell of Pottsville, PA, was traveling north on U.S. 56 south of U.S. 400. A 2001 Cadillac DeVille, operated by 30-year-old Jose G. Soto-Gonzalez of Dodge City, then attempted to cross U.S. 56 from Lariat Way at the intersection. The Dodge struck the Cadillac, causing the pickup to roll into the northeast ditch. After spinning from the impact, the Cadillac collided with a stationary USD 443 school bus. The bus, driven by 64-year-old Wade S. Hampton of Dodge City, was stopped on Lariat Way and headed west on U.S. 56. Stickell was taken to Western Plains Medical Center. Soto-Gonzalez, Hampton, and the nine children aboard the bus were unharmed. The KHP confirmed all drivers were properly restrained.

We live in a society where people are quite judgmental about how a woman dresses or behaves. Sadly, in our country, a smoking and tattooed women are still considered promiscuous.
Kriti Sanon is all set to question this stigma with her role of Bitti in her upcoming film Bareilly Ki Barfi. Talking about it, the actress was quoted as saying, "Smoking is not good for health and should be avoided. I am a non-smoker, but the point we want to make is that girls who smoke, who are fond of body art or break into a jig are not characterless."
She further added, "Our society has a very small bracket for 'good girls'. That bracket needs to broaden up or change. When a guy is moophat or smokes, he is not considered characterless, but you judge girls too fast. This is seen more in smaller towns. In an arranged marriage too, only a girl is asked all kinds of questions. I really want this to change."
On the other hand, Kriti's alleged relationship with Sushant Singh Rajput has been grabbing headlines time and again. Recently while talking to a leading daily, here's what she had to say-
"Gone are the days when enjoying a movie or dinner with a co-star would be called a date. There is nothing wrong in being friends with your co-actors and if that involves dinners or movies, why not? It's sad if I stop socialising with a friend, just because people are cooking up stories. I am not answerable to any one. I would still hang out with my male friends and people can assume anything they like. As for Sushant, I don't have control over what people talk about us. I have already spoken enough about it."
Directed by Ashwiny Iyer Tiwary, Bareilly Ki Barfi also stars Ayushmann Khurrana and Rajkummar Rao and is slated to release this week.
rewrite:
In our society, women often face harsh judgment based on their appearance or actions. It remains unfortunate that in many parts of the country, a woman with tattoos or one who smokes is still unfairly labeled as promiscuous. Kriti Sanon aims to challenge this very stigma through her character Bitti in the upcoming film *Bareilly Ki Barfi*. Addressing the issue, the actress stated, "While smoking is unhealthy and should be avoided—I myself am a non-smoker—the point is that girls who smoke, enjoy body art, or love to dance are not without character."

She elaborated further, noting that society maintains a narrow definition of a "good girl," a concept that urgently requires broadening or transformation. "A man who is straightforward or smokes isn’t deemed characterless, yet girls are judged too quickly. This mindset is more prevalent in smaller towns. Even in arranged marriages, only the girl faces an interrogation. I truly wish to see this change," Kriti expressed.

Apart from her professional role, Kriti’s speculated relationship with co-star Sushant Singh Rajput has repeatedly made news. In a recent interview, she addressed the rumors: "The era when sharing a movie or meal with a colleague was instantly called a date is over. There’s nothing wrong with being friends with fellow actors, and if that includes dinners or films, so be it. It would be regrettable to avoid socializing with a friend simply due to fabricated stories. I am not accountable to anyone; I will continue spending time with my male friends, and people may assume what they wish. Regarding Sushant, I cannot control public speculation. I have said all I need to on the matter."

Scheduled for release this week, *Bareilly Ki Barfi* is directed by Ashwiny Iyer Tiwary and also features Ayushmann Khurrana and Rajkummar Rao.

Yemenis check the damage in the aftermath of a reported air strike by the Saudi-led coalition in the Yemeni capital Sana'a on March 8, 2018. AFP
The US Senate has teed up a vote on ending the US military involvement in the Saudi war on Yemen.
Spearheaded by Senators Bernie Sanders, Mike Lee and Chris Murphy, the resolution would not include the US alleged targeting of al-Qaeda elements in the impoverished country, Press TV reported.
Once the Senate reconvenes on Tuesday, the lawmakers could have up to four hours of debate; therefore, a vote is expected at approximately 4:15 pm.
If passed, the measure would require all US forces to leave the war-ravaged country within 30 days.
"You know it's a new precedent. ... I think a lot of members on our side are trying to figure out what a yes vote means and what a no vote means," Texas Republican Senator John Cornyn told The Hill.
Lawmakers from both sides of the aisle have already voiced opposition for the US support for Riyadh, implicated in war crimes in the neighboring country, but it is still unclear whether the effort could garner enough votes.
rewrite: On March 8, 2018, Yemenis in the capital Sana'a surveyed the damage from a reported air strike conducted by the Saudi-led coalition. A vote to end U.S. military involvement in the Saudi-led war in Yemen is now pending in the U.S. Senate. According to Press TV, the resolution, championed by Senators Bernie Sanders, Mike Lee, and Chris Murphy, would specifically exclude U.S. operations allegedly targeting al-Qaeda elements within the impoverished nation. When the Senate reconvenes Tuesday, lawmakers will have up to four hours for debate, with a vote anticipated around 4:15 p.m. Should it pass, the measure mandates the withdrawal of all U.S. forces from the war-ravaged country within 30 days. Senator John Cornyn, a Texas Republican, remarked to The Hill, "You know it's a new precedent... I think a lot of members on our side are trying to figure out what a yes vote means and what a no vote means." While lawmakers from both parties have expressed opposition to U.S. support for Riyadh—implicated in war crimes in Yemen—it remains uncertain whether the resolution will secure sufficient votes.

Former Dortmund coach and eye witness Thomas Tuchel arrives at the trial against Sergej W., no family name given due to German privacy laws, who is charged with detonating three bombs targeting the Borussia Dortmund soccer team bus last April, at the German state court in Dortmund, Germany, Monday March 19, 2018.the trial (Bernd Thissen/dpa via AP)
Former Dortmund coach and eye witness Thomas Tuchel arrives at the trial against Sergej W., no family name given due to German privacy laws, who is charged with detonating three bombs targeting the Borussia Dortmund soccer team bus last April, at the German state court in Dortmund, Germany, Monday March 19, 2018.the trial (Bernd Thissen/dpa via AP)
BERLIN (AP) - Borussia Dortmund's ex-coach Thomas Tuchel has testified at the trial of a man accused of bombing the German soccer club's bus that the attack was partly responsible for his departure.
Defender Marc Bartra and a police officer were hurt in the April 11 attack as the bus left a Dortmund hotel for a Champions League match against Monaco. Dortmund played, and lost, the game a day later.
The dpa news agency reported Tuchel suggested Monday at suspect Sergei W.'s trial that the attack led to a disagreement with chief executive Hans-Joachim Watzke over rescheduling the game, probably because "I was sitting in the bus and he wasn't."
Tuchel says it was a mistake to schedule the match a day later.
Tuchel was fired in May after an inconsistent season.
rewrite:
On Monday, March 19, 2018, former Borussia Dortmund coach Thomas Tuchel arrived at a German state court in Dortmund as an eyewitness. He was there for the trial of a man identified only as Sergej W., in accordance with German privacy laws. The defendant faces charges for detonating three bombs targeting the Dortmund team bus in April of the previous year.

During his testimony, Tuchel stated that the attack was a factor in his eventual departure from the club. The bombing occurred on April 11 as the bus departed a hotel for a Champions League match against Monaco, injuring defender Marc Bartra and a police officer. The match was postponed and played a day later, a decision Tuchel called a mistake.

According to reports from the dpa news agency, Tuchel suggested the attack caused a disagreement with club CEO Hans-Joachim Watzke over rescheduling the game. He implied this rift arose because, as he noted, "I was sitting in the bus and he wasn’t." Tuchel was dismissed in May following a season of inconsistent results.

Birmingham City have made an offer to former England and Chelsea defender John Terry.
Blues boss Harry Redknapp revealed the news on talkSPORT this morning.
The ex-England captain is available on a free transfer this summer having ended his 22-year association with Chelsea.
He is understood to have interest from Premier League sides Bournemouth and West Brom while Aston Villa have also been linked, but Redknapp hopes to convince the veteran centre back to come to St Andrew's.
Speaking to the Alan Brazil Sports Breakfast the Blues boss said: “I’d love to have him at the football club.
“He’s a fantastic captain and great leader.
“We’ve made him a good offer and we have done the best we can. It’s up to John now, but we would love him at Birmingham.”
Redknapp insists that even at 36-years-old Terry still has something to offer.
“He played for me the other week in Michael Carrick’s testimonial. Fergie had the 2008 Champions League-winning team, I had an All-Star team and I had John at the back with Jamie Carragher - and I would have them two together all day long. They were fantastic.
“I had a chat with him and said to him come in - he’s doing his coaching badges - have a year or two and who knows what he wants to do in the future?”

Birmingham City have submitted an offer to former England and Chelsea captain John Terry, as confirmed by Blues manager Harry Redknapp during an appearance on talkSPORT. Terry is currently a free agent following the conclusion of his long-term tenure with Chelsea, which spanned 22 years. While Premier League clubs Bournemouth and West Brom are reportedly interested, and Aston Villa have also been mentioned as a potential destination, Redknapp is aiming to persuade the veteran defender to join Birmingham City at St Andrew's.

Speaking to the Alan Brazil Sports Breakfast, Redknapp expressed his strong desire to bring Terry to the club. "I’d love to have him at the football club. He’s a fantastic captain and great leader," said the Blues boss. He added, "We’ve made him a good offer and we have done the best we can. It’s up to John now, but we would love him at Birmingham."

Redknapp emphasized that Terry, despite being 36, still has significant value to offer. He referenced Terry's recent performance in Michael Carrick’s testimonial match, where Terry played in an All-Star team alongside Jamie Carragher against a side managed by Sir Alex Ferguson. "They were fantastic. I would have them two together all day long," Redknapp noted. The manager also revealed a conversation with Terry, suggesting he could combine playing with pursuing his coaching badges for a year or two, leaving his future options open.

A COMMUNITY day has been arranged to spread awareness of a disability benefit campaign.
The free event, which will be held at Set The Bar next to Wrexham Bus Station, will take place from 1pm to 11pm tomorrow in aid of the Save The Welsh Independent Living Campaign (SWILG).
There will be a number of performances throughout the day including Wrexham One World Community Choir, Luke Gallagher, Jamie Hamilton and more.
Disability campaigner Nathan Lee Davies is encouraging residents to turn out and support the event, which is expected to draw visitors from all over North Wales.
He said: “SWILG is an absolutely vital movement and a campaign that must be won.
“I implore people to come along to our completely free community day and I would encourage everyone to get involved with us on this SWILG campaign.
“We currently have a fantastic exhibition on in Theatre Clwyd, Mold, which we are proud to have put together.
“People such as the film-maker Ken Loach, to performers like Attila The Stockbroker, to some English and Welsh MPs and AMs, to Welsh Labour Grassroots/
Momentum to the local Labour parties in Clwyd South and Wrexham have given their full, official support.
“I cannot tell you how much that means to me and thousands like me.
“As I say, this is a campaign we simply cannot afford to lose.”
The Welsh Government became responsible for supporting those who had been receiving Independent Living Fund payments after the UK government closed the scheme in June 2015.
According to the charity Disability Rights UK, Welsh Independent Living Grant funding will continue during 2017-2018, but local councils will meet with the people receiving them to discuss the replacement support they need – by March 31, 2019, all recipients will receive their support from local councils.
To find out more about the campaign, search for @SaveWILG on Facebook.
For more information about the community day, search for the event 'Save the Welsh Independent Living Grant (SWILG) Community Day' on Facebook.
rewrite:
A free community day aimed at raising awareness for the Save The Welsh Independent Living Campaign (SWILG) is scheduled for tomorrow. Running from 1pm to 11pm at Set The Bar, located next to Wrexham Bus Station, the event will feature a variety of performances. These include acts by the Wrexham One World Community Choir, Luke Gallagher, and Jamie Hamilton, among others. Disability campaigner Nathan Lee Davies is urging residents to attend and support the gathering, which is anticipated to attract visitors from across North Wales.

Davies emphasized the critical nature of the cause, stating, “SWILG is an absolutely vital movement and a campaign that must be won.” He added, “I implore people to come along to our completely free community day and I would encourage everyone to get involved with us on this SWILG campaign.” He also highlighted a currently running exhibition at Theatre Clwyd in Mold, which the campaign is proud to have organized. The campaign has garnered significant official backing from a diverse range of supporters, including film-maker Ken Loach, performer Attila The Stockbroker, various English and Welsh MPs and AMs, Welsh Labour Grassroots/Momentum, and local Labour parties in Clwyd South and Wrexham. “I cannot tell you how much that means to me and thousands like me,” Davies expressed. “As I say, this is a campaign we simply cannot afford to lose.”

The context for this campaign stems from the Welsh Government assuming responsibility for supporting former recipients of the Independent Living Fund after its closure by the UK government in June 2015. According to Disability Rights UK, funding through the Welsh Independent Living Grant will persist through 2017-2018. However, local councils are set to meet with recipients to plan for replacement support. By March 31, 2019, all support will be administered directly by local councils. For further details on the campaign, find @SaveWILG on Facebook. More information about the community day can be located by searching for the event 'Save the Welsh Independent Living Grant (SWILG) Community Day' on the same platform.

rewrite: On May 3, Laredo Petroleum Inc. released its financial and operating results for the first quarter of 2017. The company reported quarterly production of 52,405 barrels of oil equivalent per day, marking an approximate 13% increase from the same period in 2016. For Q1, earnings per share were $0.28, while adjusted non-GAAP earnings per share came in at $0.10; the Thomson Reuters I/B/E/S consensus estimate had been $0.11. SUPER CAT: Jack Cross puts his body on the line against the Maroochydore Roos. Leeroy Todd
Aussie Rules: The Gympie Cats' clash against Bundaberg's Across the Waves last weekend resulted in the Cats disputing the final score.
After singing the club song, thinking they had secured a hard fought victory, the Cats were told they had lost the game by two points.
Cats officials recorded Gympie 12.12 (84) and Across the Waves 12.8 (80).
The goal umpires recorded Across the Waves 12.8 (80) and Cats 11.12 (78).
Cats coach and co-captain Courtney Findlay said the Cats were in the process of disputing the final score.
"We believe we kicked three goals in the final quarter but the goal umpires only recorded two,” he said.
"The papers have been lodged to AFL Queensland with proof backing up our belief. Hopefully we hear back this week.”
Gympie welcomed back Madry Tonkin who was sidelined due to a suspension from last year.
"Despite playing his first game of the season, Tonkin played well,” Findlay said.
"He was rotated through a few different positions and he handled it well.”
Cats' Jack Cross had another stand out performance, backing up from last week's game.
"He played up forward and was quiet creative,” Findlay said. "Jack won contested possessions in the midfield and when the game was to be won, he kicked a crucial goal.” Cross and Tonkin were not the only stand out Cats players; Jesse Lawrence had a great game in the midfield.
Cats head back to Bundaberg this Saturday to play Brothers Bulldogs at 3pm at Brothers AFL complex.
rewrite:
In a contentious Aussie Rules match last weekend, the Gympie Cats disputed the final score following their clash with Bundaberg’s Across the Waves. Initially celebrating what they believed was a hard-fought victory after singing the club song, the Cats were later informed they had actually lost by two points. While Cats officials recorded a score of Gympie 12.12 (84) to Across the Waves 12.8 (80), the goal umpires’ tally showed Across the Waves 12.8 (80) and the Cats 11.12 (78). According to Cats coach and co-captain Courtney Findlay, the team is challenging the outcome. “We believe we kicked three goals in the final quarter, but the goal umpires only recorded two,” he stated, adding that paperwork with supporting evidence had been lodged with AFL Queensland, and a response is hoped for this week.

The match saw the return of Madry Tonkin, who had been sidelined by a suspension from last year. Findlay noted that despite it being Tonkin’s first game of the season, he performed well, adapting effectively as he was rotated through several positions. Another standout was Jack Cross, who built on his strong performance from the previous week. Playing creatively up forward, Cross won contested possessions in the midfield and sealed his impact by kicking a crucial goal when the game was on the line. Jesse Lawrence also delivered an excellent performance in the midfield, rounding out the Cats’ notable contributors. Looking ahead, the Cats return to Bundaberg this Saturday to face the Brothers Bulldogs at 3 p.m. at the Brothers AFL complex.

Leeds United were prepared to include a clause in any loan deal for Juventus striker Moise Kean that would have seen the Whites automatically buy the hitman in the event of promotion to the Premier League.
The Whites went shopping for a young striker in the January transfer window and eventually signed Tyler Roberts from West Brom for an initial £2.5m.
However, before focusing in on the 19-year-old, Leeds made a play to sign Kean, who is on loan at Hellas Verona from Juventus.
The Championship side wanted to take Kean on loan until the end of the season and let Juventus know they would cover his full salary.
Also, according to Italian outlet Calciomercato.com, the Whites were also willing to guarantee they would sign Kean on a permanent transfer at the end of the season if they won promotion to the Premier League.
Leeds agreed a similar deal with Villarreal for winger Alfonso Pedraza in the 2017 January window, but the player returned to Spain last summer with the Whites having missed out on promotion.
Juventus were not moved by Leeds' proposal for Kean and are now actively including the 17-year-old in their plans going forward.
Kean grabbed a brace for Hellas Verona in their 4-1 win at Fiorentina in his last appearance for the club.
rewrite: During the January transfer window, Leeds United sought to strengthen their attack by targeting a young striker, ultimately securing Tyler Roberts from West Brom for an initial £2.5 million. Prior to finalizing that move, however, they attempted to arrange a loan for Juventus forward Moise Kean, who is currently at Hellas Verona. The Championship club’s proposal included covering Kean’s full salary for the remainder of the season. Additionally, as reported by Calciomercato.com, Leeds were prepared to insert a clause guaranteeing a permanent transfer should they achieve promotion to the Premier League. This structure mirrored a previous deal with Villarreal for Alfonso Pedraza in January 2017, though that loan ended with the player’s return after Leeds failed to gain promotion. Juventus, unmoved by Leeds’ offer, are now integrating the 17-year-old Kean into their long-term plans. Kean recently impressed by scoring twice in Hellas Verona’s 4-1 victory over Fiorentina.

A racist manspreader assaulted a woman on the subway because she asked him to give her a bit more room to sit down, police said Saturday.
The 34-year-old victim was seated inside a northbound E train on Tuesday at around 5: 10 pm when the man sat down, partially on top of her, police said.
When she asked him to move for a moment so she could readjust herself, he shouted: “Just because you’re African American, you think you can go on your Kanye West rant, you black b***h,” according to cops, who have released an image of the suspect.
Later, as the woman was preparing to exit the train, she bumped his bag, prompting him to spit on the back of her head, said police.
The matter escalated even further when both passengers left at the 7th Avenue stop in Manhattan. When she grabbed the man’s backpack to confront him, he punched her in the shoulder and spit in her face again, and then fled back onto the train, police said.
Police describe the man as white-Hispanic, in his 30s, and approximately 5-foot-9 and 150 pounds.
