(WFLA) – Wresting Hall of Famer Ric Flair remained hospitalized Monday as his representative made a public plea for prayers.
Over the weekend, Pro Wrestling Sheet reported that the WWE champion had been admitted to a hospital for heart-related issues.
Late Sunday night, Flair’s representative, Melinda Morris Zanoni with Legacy Talent, asked for prayers and positive energy for the wrestler.
“Are u a Fan/Friend of Ric Flair?If so, we need prayers & positive energy 4 our Living Legend as he is dealing w/some tough medical issues,” she said.
On Saturday, she tweeted that the wrestler was in the hospital.
“Yes,Ric in hosp 4routine monitoring.No reason2panic.Yes,many thx2his fiancé&hospstaff.No excuses Ric wld want u2go out 2nite NaturBoy style!”
Flair, age 68, gained fame as a big time wrestler in the late 1970s along with several other wrestlers such as Hulk Hogan, Andre the Giant and ‘Macho Man’ Randy Savage. Flair was especially popular for his antics.
Flair was inducted into the WWE Hall of Fame in 2008 and retired after a 36-year career.According to his website, Ric Flair’s robe, his trunks, and the boots he wore at Wrestlemania XXIV, are all on exhibit at the Smithsonian National Museum of American History in Washington DC.
rewrite:
Ric Flair, a 68-year-old WWE Hall of Famer renowned for his flamboyant antics and career alongside legends like Hulk Hogan, remained hospitalized on Monday. His representative, Melinda Morris Zanoni of Legacy Talent, issued a public plea for prayers and positive energy late Sunday night. She asked fans and friends to support "our Living Legend as he is dealing w/some tough medical issues." This followed earlier reports over the weekend from Pro Wrestling Sheet that the former champion had been admitted for heart-related concerns.

Zanoni had initially tweeted on Saturday, stating Flair was in the hospital for "routine monitoring" and urged no panic, even humorously suggesting he would want people to go out "NaturBoy style." Flair rose to fame in the late 1970s and enjoyed a 36-year career before retiring and receiving his Hall of Fame induction in 2008. His legacy is further cemented by artifacts from his career, including his robe, trunks, and boots from Wrestlemania XXIV, which are displayed at the Smithsonian National Museum of American History in Washington, D.C.

General News of Friday, 6 October 2017
Source: Starrfmonline.com
2017-10-06
Sophia Akuffo, Chief Justice
The Chief Justice Sophia Akuffo has bemoaned the growing indiscipline at the BAR of Ghana as she charges newly enrolled lawyers to be of good behaviour.
According to Justice Akuffo, the high level of indiscipline amongst lawyers in Ghana is alarming and disappointing.
Addressing 208 newly enrolled lawyers to the Ghana BAR at the enrollment ceremony held at the Banquet Hall of the State House Friday, the Chief Justice said the Disciplinary Committee of the General Legal Council (GLC) is overwhelmed by the several misconduct complaints against lawyers.
She charged the newly enrolled lawyers to uphold all the rules governing the Profession they have chosen.
“We are witnessing these days a distressing increase in a number of disciplinary complaints that come before the disciplinary committee of the General Legal Council against lawyers especially the younger ones at the BAR.
“The root cause of most of these is lack of self-discipline and the desire to get rich quick on the part of new lawyers,” the Chief Justice said on Friday.
Justice Akuffo called on the lawyers to at all times observe the rules and ensure that none of them ever appears before the disciplinary committee of the General Legal Council.
rewrite:
On Friday, October 6, 2017, Chief Justice Sophia Akuffo addressed 208 newly enrolled lawyers at a ceremony held in the State House Banquet Hall. She expressed deep concern over the alarming and disappointing rise in indiscipline within the Ghanaian BAR. Justice Akuffo stated that the Disciplinary Committee of the General Legal Council (GLC) is currently overwhelmed by numerous misconduct complaints filed against legal practitioners.

The Chief Justice specifically bemoaned a distressing increase in complaints, particularly involving younger lawyers. She identified the root causes as a lack of self-discipline and a pervasive desire among new entrants to amass wealth quickly. In her charge to the newly enrolled lawyers, she urged them to uphold all the professional rules governing their chosen career.

Justice Akuffo emphasized the importance of good behavior, calling on the lawyers to consistently observe the established regulations. Her ultimate charge was for each new lawyer to ensure they never appear before the GLC's Disciplinary Committee, thereby upholding the integrity and discipline of the legal profession in Ghana.

Derby County will be hoping to pit their wits against Premier League champions Chelsea next season.
The Rams are looking to end their 10-year exile from the top flight, and are currently on course to do so – occupying the second automatic promotion spot in the Championship.
Chelsea are notorious for loaning out a vast amount of their young players – with the club’s official website stating they have 37 players out on loan, the latest being Kasey Palmer who joined Derby County on transfer deadline day.
High-profile names include Tammy Abraham, Kurt Zouma and Lewis Baker, while a lot of the Academy prospects are also out getting first-team experience.
Derby can draw comparison to that – albeit on a lesser scale.
Deadline day loan deals for Chris Martin and Mason Bennett meant that the Rams currently have 17 players out on loan.
(Image: Jason Dawson/ Reading Football Club)
They range from first-team stalwarts, to youngsters looking to further their current Under-23 experience.
First-teamers Jacob Butterfield and Craig Bryson joined Sheffield Wednesday and Cardiff City in the summer – while Jason Shackell and Darren Bent are at Millwall and Burton Albion.
Shackell and Bent have left this window, along with Max Lowe, Charles Vernam, Callum Guy, Offrande Zanzala, Emil Jakobsen, Martin and Bennett.
Alex Cover (Alfreton), Kyron Stabana (Boston), Kelle Roos (Plymouth) have also all spent time out on loan. Farrend Rawson was on loan at Accrington before his permanent move to Forest Green Rovers.
Here’s a full list of the players currently out on loan:

Craig Bryson – Cardiff City

rewrite:
Derby County currently find themselves positioned to secure automatic promotion from the Championship, aiming to conclude a decade-long absence from the Premier League. Should they succeed, a matchup with reigning champions Chelsea could await. Chelsea are widely recognized for their extensive loan system, with the club listing 37 players currently gaining experience elsewhere. Notable among these are Tammy Abraham, Kurt Zouma, and Lewis Baker, alongside numerous academy prospects seeking first-team action.

On a smaller scale, Derby County employs a similar strategy. The recent loan departures of Chris Martin and Reading’s Mason Bennett on transfer deadline day brought the Rams' total to 17 players currently out on loan. This group encompasses both established first-team figures and younger talents aiming to build upon their Under-23 development.

Several senior players departed on loan during the summer window. Jacob Butterfield moved to Sheffield Wednesday, while Craig Bryson joined Cardiff City. More recently, the January transfer window saw further exits, including Jason Shackell to Millwall, Darren Bent to Burton Albion, and Max Lowe to Shrewsbury Town. Other players who have left on loan include Charles Vernam (Grimsby Town), Callum Guy (Bradford City), Offrande Zanzala (Accrington Stanley), and Emil Jakobsen (VVV Venlo).

Additional players who have spent time on loan this season are Alex Cover (Alfreton Town), Kyron Stabana (Boston United), and Kelle Roos (Plymouth Argyle). Farrend Rawson was previously on loan at Accrington Stanley before making a permanent transfer to Forest Green Rovers.

The complete list of Derby County players currently out on loan is as follows: Jacob Butterfield (Sheffield Wednesday), Craig Bryson (Cardiff City), Timi Max Elsnik (Swindon Town), Kellan Gordon (Swindon Town), Calum Macdonald (Barrow), Nick Blackman (Maccabi Tel Aviv), Henrich Ravas (Gainsborough Trinity), Matthew Taylor (Gainsborough Trinity), Max Lowe (Shrewsbury Town), Charles Vernam (Grimsby Town), Callum Guy (Bradford City), Offrande Zanzala (Accrington Stanley), Emil Jakobsen (VVV Venlo), Jason Shackell (Millwall), Darren Bent (Burton Albion), Chris Martin (Reading), and Mason Bennett (Notts County).

This loan approach mirrors, in a more modest fashion, the model used by clubs like Chelsea, who notably sent Kasey Palmer to Derby on deadline day.

Crawley Town player Lewis Young has signed a new contract which will run until the end of the 2019-20 season.
Head coach Harry Kewell said: “We’re delighted that Youngy is on board for the next two seasons. He’s a great professional and very popular with our fans.
“I like to think he improved last season. We got him to play a slightly different role which he adapted really well to and, of course, he’s now a goalscorer as well!
“Hopefully with his experience he can help us push on next season and beyond and I’m pleased he is going to be part of what we’re trying to achieve.”
The defender/wing-back, who is aged 28, is one of the longest-serving members of the squad, having joined Reds in 2015.
He has since played 173 league and cup games for the club, scoring three goals.

Head coach Harry Kewell expressed his delight, stating, “We’re delighted that Youngy is on board for the next two seasons. He’s a great professional and very popular with our fans.” Kewell noted the player's adaptation to a modified role last season and his development into a goalscorer. He added, “Hopefully with his experience he can help us push on next season and beyond and I’m pleased he is going to be part of what we’re trying to achieve.”
